insights.title: Activate to accumulate: NIQ reveals the power of On-Premise activations Insights from NIQ reveals the power of activations in Britain’s On-Premise—but with spending tight and competition fierce, brands have to work hard to get noticed. According to NIQ’s latest BrandTrack research, more than two thirds (69%) of consumers are more likely to try a drink they have not had before if they see a brand activation. A similar proportion (68%) say activations positively impact their perception of the brand involved.  Crucially, these enhancements to brand reputation translate directly into commercial outcomes. Two in three (66%) consumers say they are more likely to order a brand when it features in an activation.  Why visibility is critical to converting consumers Lasting impacts  BrandTrack shows how On-Premise activity can trigger spending in the Off-Premise as well. Nearly two thirds (64%) of consumers say activations increase their likelihood of purchasing a brand later in a supermarket—a reminder that pubs and bars are vital channels for generating trial and loyalty.  Activations can benefit operators as well as suppliers. More than thee in five consumers say activations make them more likely to go into a venue (63%) or to revisit it again in the future (62%). It’s clear that good collaborations can bring positive outcomes for brands and venues alike.  The attention challenge NIQ’s BrandTrack solution provides a wealth of insights to help brand owners and operators understand consumers’ attitudes to activations and tackle the core challenge of securing their attention. The latest data shows that around a third of consumers (34%) have never noticed a branded drinks activation in a pub, bar or restaurant. On top of that, well over a quarter (29%) don’t recall seeing one within the last month, while a quarter (25%) can’t remember the last time they saw one. Just 6% have noticed an activation in the last week. While activations can be a powerful tool for drinks brands, many are currently failing to reach consumers at scale or make a lasting impression on them.  “Activations can be a hugely effective tool for brand owners and venue operators alike. With so much choice at the bar, compelling activity can make all the difference to trial, brand equity and commercial success. However, many activations aren’t landing as well as they could. Fixing the lack of penetration, and making activations eye-catching and memorable, have to be top priorities for all stakeholders. With consumers increasingly looking for experiences rather than simple purchases, brands that craft standout activations can achieve a vital head start in the race for sales.” Lou Finn - Senior Consumer Research Executive – NielsenIQ   Learn more NIQ’s BrandTrack solution is based on a quarterly survey of 5,000 nationally representative British consumers. It delivers outstanding insights into the behaviours of pub, bar and restaurant guests, including their attitudes to several hundred eating and drinking out brands. Bespoke analysis is available to help businesses identify the core components of activations and other brand activity, and assess their performance against competitors. To learn more, get in touch. insights.title: Drinks sales pick up in September after tough August Average sales in managed venues in the week to Saturday 5 September were 7.6% ahead of the same week in 2025, thanks to a combination of good weather and the August Bank Holiday weekend. This was followed by solid growth of 2.5% in the next seven days to Saturday 12 September.  The upswing comes after a difficult August, when extreme heat kept some people away from the On-Premise. Sales in the week to Saturday 29 August fell 9.7% behind the same week last August. It was a sixth straight negative weekly number since the end of the football World Cup in mid-July, during which fans spent freely in pubs and bars. The Daily Drinks Tracker, powered by CGA intelligence, indicates that the first fortnight of September was particularly strong for Long Alcoholic Drinks (LAD) suppliers, as consumers sought refreshment from long serves. Beer sales were up by 8.4% and 5.7% in the weeks to 5 and 12 September respectively. Cider fared even better, leaping by 13.3% and 7.3%. These two categories were also boosted by an attractive programme of football fixtures in the Premier League and Champions League.   It was also a good two weeks for soft drinks, which rose by 11.9% and 4.6% across the fortnight. However, wine (up 2.9% and down 6.0%) and spirits (up 0.8% and down 16.5%) were weaker.  The Tracker’s daily breakdown of trading shows a particularly buoyant August Bank Holiday weekend. Sales on Sunday and Monday (30 and 31 August) jumped 39.3% and 59.4% ahead of the same days in 2025, though these comparisons are skewed by an earlier Bank Holiday in 2025. Wednesday 9 September (up 15.9%) and Thursday 10 September (up 8.9%) were two other standout days.  After a good start to September, trading slipped back in the third week of the month as cooler and wetter weather moved into many parts of Britain. Average sales in the seven days to Saturday 19 September were 2.0% down on the corresponding week in 2025. Rachel Weller, NIQ’s commercial lead, UK & Ireland, said: “A good start to September will have been a relief to On-Premise operators and beer, cider and soft drinks brands. It has helped to claw back some of the ground that was lost in August, when extreme heatwaves, a World Cup hangover and consumers’ watchful spending made for a difficult environment. Nevertheless, conditions are likely to remain very challenging as we move towards the crucial final quarter of the year. A lot now hangs on the government’s Budget in October, which is a crucial opportunity to revive the confidence of consumers and hospitality alike.”“A good start to September will have been a relief to On-Premise operators and beer, cider and soft drinks brands. insights.title: Hospitality in 2026: Calm or chaos? Why flat headline figures hide rapid market change Flat sites and sales  NIQ’s data shows how key On-Premise metrics have remained static this year. They include the number of licensed premises, which dropped by just 0.2% in the 12 months to June, according to the Hospitality Market Monitor.  Sales have been essentially unchanged too. The NIQ RSM Hospitality Business Tracker shows like-for-like sales for managed pub, restaurant and bar groups have hovered less than 2 percentage points either side of zero in every month of 2026 so far. This is slightly below Britain’s rate of inflation as measured by the Consumer Prices Index, but real-terms growth has tracked just above it, thanks to modest but steady new openings by some operators.  Similarly, consumers’ levels of visitation and spend are virtually unchanged. NIQ’s BrandTrack data indicates that 42% of consumers went out to eat weekly in the first half of 2026—just 1 percentage point fewer than 12 months earlier. Average spend per head stood at £24.49, which is just 24 pence more than in the first half of 2025.  Churn and change  However, while things appear calm on the surface of hospitality, there’s a lot of turbulence underneath. Headline On-Premise numbers may be stationary, but there’s been a 7% churn in sites in the last 12 months. A total of 3,885 venues have closed, but 3,703 have opened as entrepreneurs and groups take advantage of vacant premises. It is a sign of both the fragility of hospitality and the underlying confidence in the sector among operators and investors. Turnover has been even faster in late-night channels. The Night Time Economy Market Monitor from NIQ and the Night Time Industries Association reveals nearly one in five bars and nightclubs either entering or exiting the market in the last 12 months. This is a consequence of one of hospitality’s most significant dynamics of recent times: consumers’ desire to go out earlier. According to NIQ’s Trading Index, the early evening period of 5pm to 7pm now generates more sales than the late evening slot of 7pm to 10pm. It is a trend with major implications for pubs, bars and clubs and their suppliers.  New value demands  Earlier visits are just one element among more widely shifting behavioural trends. Ongoing cost of living impacts, and increasing hospitality prices, are redefining value for money in the eyes of the consumer. But while there are some signs of a drawback from the most expensive product categories, there is a simultaneous elevation of the minimum quality consumers find acceptable, as consumers at either end of the spectrum seek experiences that they can justify spending on.  Beyond quality and cost, the demand for an all-round experience continues to rise. This is also contributing to a consumer withdrawal from casual visits, with spend redirected towards more immersive and shared occasions.  Squeezed spending may also be leading consumers to swap eating out for ordering in, as NIQ’s Hospitality Business Tracker shows restaurants have achieved better growth in deliveries and takeaways throughout 2026. What’s coming next?  Predicting what’s around the corner for hospitality isn’t easy. Leaders remain concerned about the future, with NIQ’s latest Business Confidence Survey showing just 35% of them are optimistic about prospects for their business over the next 12 months. However, there are some grounds for very cautious optimism, as confidence levels jumped sharply after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced support for pubs and clubs on rates in July. Nearly half (47%) of leaders were optimistic that the change in government would benefit the hospitality and brewing industry.  The big test of that confidence comes on Wednesday 28 October, when the government unveils its Budget. After such a turbulent year, it could be a make-or-break moment for weakened businesses, ahead of what should be the most profitable two months of the year for the sector.  Track Britain’s evolving Hospitality market NIQ’s suite of business and consumer research solutions provides outstanding insights into current and future trends in Britain’s On-Premise. insights.title: The End of Pantry Loading: Why CPGs Must Rethink Packaging Architecture for the New American Shopper For decades, CPG growth strategies have been built around a simple assumption: consumers want more. More value, larger pack sizes, bigger baskets, and fully stocked pantries. But today's shopper is changing. Smaller households, rising living costs, changing family structures, increased omnichannel shopping, and the growing adoption of GLP-1 medications are fundamentally reshaping how consumers purchase, store, and consume products. The traditional pantry-loading model is becoming less relevant as shoppers prioritize affordability, convenience, portion control, and waste reduction. As Gen X, Millennials, Gen Z, and Boomers move through dramatically different life stages and household structures, manufacturers and retailers have an opportunity to rethink packaging architecture, promotional strategies, and value propositions for the next generation of shoppers. insights.title: The Real Story Behind Consumer Polarization in AME Africa and the Middle East's FMCG sector continues to deliver impressive growth on paper. Regional FMCG value sales grew 13.7% in the 12 months to Q2 2026. But beneath that headline lies a more complex reality. Volume growth reached just 3.7%, while unit value growth accounted for 10.0% of market expansion, highlighting a marketplace where consumer behavior is becoming increasingly fragmented. For manufacturers and retailers, the biggest risk today is assuming consumers fit neatly into traditional segments. The idea of the "premium shopper" and the "value shopper" is becoming less relevant. Across markets, the same consumer may willingly pay more in some categories while actively seeking savings in others. The traditional idea of targeting the "average consumer" is also becoming less useful. As consumers increasingly move between premium and value choices depending on category, occasion, need state, and perceived value, brands can no longer assume consistent purchasing behavior across the basket. The real shift isn't that consumers are spending more or less. It's that they're becoming more selective about what deserves their money and what doesn't. Three Consumer Realities Shaping FMCG Growth Headline growth figures often suggest a single story, but consumer behavior tells a different one. Across markets, three realities are emerging simultaneously. Some consumers continue to navigate inflationary pressures and rising living costs. Others are benefiting from stronger purchasing power and increasing consumption. And in several markets, household budgets remain under significant strain, forcing difficult trade-offs between essential and discretionary spending. What makes this particularly interesting is that these different circumstances are producing a surprisingly similar outcome: consumers are becoming far more deliberate about where they spend, where they save, and what they believe is worth paying more for. Morocco provides one example of this dynamic. FMCG value growth reached 14.5%, while volume expanded by 16.4%, driven by strong demand across beverages and ambient food. This is a market where consumers continue to increase consumption despite minimal inflation. The UAE reflects a different but equally telling trend. While FMCG growth remains healthy at 5.4%, consumers are increasingly shifting spending toward essential categories such as Ambient Food and Beverages, away from more discretionary purchases. Even in a relatively resilient market, consumers are becoming more intentional about where value matters most. Meanwhile, markets such as Egypt are sitting somewhere in between. As inflation eases and consumer confidence gradually improves, FMCG growth is increasingly moving away from purely inflation-driven expansion and toward more sustainable demand-led growth. At the other end of the spectrum, consumers in Saudi Arabia and Nigeria continue to face greater pressure. In Saudi Arabia, FMCG value and volume sales both declined by roughly 1%, while Nigerian consumers reduced discretionary spending and focused increasingly on essential purchases as volumes fell 1.5%. The circumstances may differ, but the underlying consumer behavior is remarkably similar. Shoppers are becoming more intentional about the value they expect from every purchase. While the behavior may be increasingly consistent, the route to growth is not. In some markets, growth comes from premiumization and higher-value propositions. In others, it comes from affordability, accessibility, distribution, or stronger participation in essential categories. Understanding which levers matter most remains highly market and category specific. The Consumer Is Not Polarized. Their Decisions Are. Much of the conversation around consumers today focuses on whether they are trading up or trading down. The evidence increasingly suggests they are doing both. Shoppers continue to pay for products that earn their premium through quality, trust, convenience, performance, innovation, or relevance. At the same time, they are increasingly willing to switch brands or choose lower-priced alternatives when the added value is less clear. Increasingly, consumers are protecting purchases that feel meaningful, functional, trusted, or personally relevant, while optimizing purchases where the premium no longer feels justified. As a result, the same shopper may actively seek value in one category while willingly paying more in another. This dynamic creates significant pressure on products positioned in the middle. The challenge is not that consumers have become unwilling to spend. Rather, they have become less willing to spend without a compelling reason. Evidence of this shift can be seen across multiple markets. In Lebanon, consumers are becoming increasingly price sensitive and more willing to switch brands in pursuit of better value. In Kuwait, private label sales surged 18.4%, reflecting growing consumer acceptance of value-oriented alternatives. In Oman and Qatar, private label continues to gain momentum, particularly across staple food categories where functionality can outweigh brand differentiation. These shifts are not necessarily signs of consumers abandoning brands. They are signs of consumers reassessing where brands genuinely add value.  Premium and value segments continue to gain share while the middle tier loses ground, illustrating that consumers are not simply trading down. They are becoming more selective about where a premium is justified and where value is sufficient.  Why E-commerce Is Accelerating the Shift Nowhere is this behavior more visible than online. E-commerce remains the fastest-growing retail channel across many markets, expanding by 37.6% in Kuwait and 26.4% in the UAE, while contributing approximately 9% of FMCG sales in Saudi Arabia. Digital commerce is doing more than creating a new route to market. It is changing how consumers evaluate value. Online shoppers can compare prices instantly, access broader assortments, review alternatives, and switch brands with minimal effort. As a result, products increasingly compete on demonstrable value rather than habit or familiarity alone. Research suggests that this environment amplifies the polarization already occurring in consumer decision-making. Online, the middle tier is often underrepresented, as shoppers gravitate toward either a clearly differentiated premium option or a compelling value alternative. Greater transparency, richer product information, wider assortments, and easier comparison make it simpler for consumers to act on those preferences. In this sense, e-commerce is not simply reflecting changing consumer behavior. It is accelerating it. Consumer polarization becomes more pronounced online, where premium and value products capture a disproportionate share of the digital basket while mid-tier products lose share. Why the Middle Is Under Growing Pressure  For many years, FMCG portfolios were built around broad, mainstream propositions designed to appeal to the largest possible audience. That model is becoming harder to sustain. The growth of private label, increased brand switching, rising price transparency, and evolving channel preferences all point in the same direction: products that cannot clearly articulate why they deserve their price are becoming increasingly vulnerable. Consumers are not rejecting premium products. They are rejecting ambiguity. A premium can still command a higher price when the benefit is clear. A value proposition can still win when affordability is the priority. The products facing the greatest pressure are those caught between the two, offering neither compelling differentiation nor a meaningful value advantage. Winning in the Era of the Contextual Consumer   The future of FMCG growth will not be determined by whether brands choose premiumization or affordability. It will depend on how effectively they understand the context behind every purchase decision. The same shopper may buy a premium infant product, a value-focused staple, a trusted heritage brand, and a private label alternative in the same basket. What matters is not whether that consumer is affluent or budget conscious. What matters is the role each product plays in their life and whether its value proposition is clear enough to justify its price. For manufacturers and retailers, this requires a deeper understanding of category dynamics, shopping missions, channel behavior, and the benefits consumers genuinely care about. The era of the average consumer is ending. Growth will increasingly come from understanding not whether consumers are trading up or trading down, but when they are willing to do either and, more importantly, why. insights.summary: Political leaders meeting at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) renewed their commitment to making the world safer from future pandemics, stressing the
insights.core: 联合国大会期间，各国政治领导人重申加强全球大流行防范的承诺，强调提升未来应对公共卫生危机的能力，虽摘要未展开具体条款，但方向明确。
insights.view: 对快消及电子烟行业而言，全球卫生安全议程升温意味着监管与合规预期将更趋严格，供应链韧性与产品安全叙事或成CMI新焦点，消费者健康敏感度亦可能持续走高。
insights.action: 建议企业提前梳理产品安全与合规风险，将公共卫生议题纳入消费者洞察追踪，并储备应急供应链与沟通预案，以应对潜在政策波动。

insights.title: Recommendations announced for influenza vaccine composition for the 2027 southern hemisphere influenza season
insights.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) today announced its recommendations for the viral composition of influenza (or ‘flu’) vaccines for use in the 20
insights.core: WHO发布2027年南半球流感疫苗毒株组成建议，为全球疫苗生产商提供下一季生产依据，属常规公共卫生预警与疫苗株更新机制。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，此洞察提示疫苗类健康产品的配方年度迭代节奏。虽非直接消费品，但其毒株更新逻辑与快消品配方调整、消费者沟通策略相通，尤其影响含健康宣称品类的市场预期管理。
insights.action: 建议关注WHO毒株建议发布节点，评估其对健康类快消品营销节奏的参照价值，并同步跟踪目标市场疫苗政策与消费者接种意愿变化。

insights.title: WHO announces expansion of prequalification programme for medical devices
insights.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) today announced a major expansion of its prequalification programme to include a wider range of life-saving medical devices
insights.core: WHO宣布扩大其医疗器械预认证计划，将覆盖更广泛范围的救生医疗器械，旨在通过统一评估标准提升全球市场准入产品的质量与可及性。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这预示医疗器械类产品的合规门槛与评价体系将趋严。若企业涉足雾化等健康相关品类，需关注预认证对产品安全、性能及用户感知标准的潜在外溢影响。
insights.action: 立即梳理自身产品线是否涉及WHO预认证范围，评估感官与消费者研究如何对接国际合规要求，提前储备安全性及性能验证数据。

insights.title: 25 September 2026 Departmental update WHO to update the recommendations on criteria and diagnosis of hyperglycaemia in pregnancy
insights.summary: One in six live births (21 million per year) is affected by hyperglycaemia during pregnancy. Hyperglycaemia in pregnancy includes diabetes that existed before p
insights.core: WHO将于2026年9月更新妊娠期高血糖的诊断标准与建议，全球每年约2100万例活产（每六例一例）受此影响，涵盖孕前糖尿病及妊娠期糖尿病。
insights.view: 该议题虽属公共卫生范畴，但对FMCG具有间接启示：妊娠期代谢健康正成为消费者关注焦点，低糖、控糖及功能性食品需求将持续升温，感官研究需关注甜味替代方案在特殊人群中的接受度与偏好。
insights.action: 建议CMI团队追踪WHO新标准落地后的舆论与消费行为变化，评估孕产妇及家庭场景下的低GI、无糖产品机会，提前布局相关感官测试与概念验证。

insights.title: 24 September 2026 Departmental update From competencies to action: strengthening refugee and migrant health
insights.summary: From 21 to 24 September 2026, policy-makers, health managers and technical experts from seven countries and territories gathered in Rome for the second Global O
insights.core: WHO于2026年9月在罗马召开第二届全球会议，汇集七个国家与地区的政策制定者、卫生管理者及技术专家，推动难民与移民健康从能力建设转向实际行动。
insights.view: 该议题表面属公共卫生，实则折射出人口结构多元化趋势。对FMCG感官与CMI而言，移民与难民群体的感官偏好、文化饮食及消费习惯正成为不可忽视的细分市场，跨文化感官接受度研究将更具战略价值。
insights.action: 建议在消费者样本库中增加移民与多元文化背景人群，开展跨文化感官偏好与接受度测试，为产品本地化与包容性创新积累一手洞察。

insights.title: 24 September 2026 Departmental update WHO-IRCH Working Group 2 advances cooperation on herbal medicine quality and standards
insights.summary: WHO convened an online workshop of the International Regulatory Cooperation for Herbal Medicines (WHO-IRCH) Working Group 2 on quality control, standardization
insights.core: WHO通过线上研讨会推进草药国际监管合作工作组（WHO-IRCH）第二组在质量控制与标准化方面的协作，聚焦草药质量标准与监管协同。
insights.view: 对快消感官与CMI而言，草药/植物基原料的质量标准趋严将外溢至食品、饮料、雾化等品类，影响风味一致性、原料合规与消费者信任叙事，需提前关注标准变动对配方与宣称的约束。
insights.action: 梳理自身产品中植物/草药类原料清单，追踪WHO-IRCH标准进展，评估对配方稳定性与感官一致性的影响，并同步更新合规与消费者沟通话术。

insights.title: America’s frustration with the cost of living continues to rise
insights.core: 益普索最新民调显示，美国民众对生活成本持续攀升的焦虑情绪进一步加剧，物价压力已成为影响消费者情绪与政治态度的核心议题，短期内未见缓解迹象。
insights.view: 对FMCG与电子雾化品类而言，这意味着消费者价格敏感度将长期高企，感官愉悦与性价比的平衡更关键；CMI需重新校准支付意愿模型，避免以单纯高端化叙事应对，转而关注小规格、多口味组合带来的感知价值。
insights.action: 建议立即在美市场启动价格弹性与感官价值感知的联合追踪，将生活成本焦虑纳入消费者分群变量，优先测试低单价入门装与高频复购场景的感官沟通策略。

insights.title: Path to Purchase Institute Future Forward
insights.core: Ipsos 主办的 Path to Purchase Institute Future Forward 活动，聚焦购买路径与未来消费趋势，面向快消与零售决策者，探讨消费者决策链路演变及数据驱动的市场洞察方法。
insights.view: 对 FMCG 感官研究与 CMI 而言，购买路径正在从线性漏斗转向碎片化、多触点循环，感官体验需与货架前、线上详情页、试用等触点联动评估。CMI 应把感官偏好数据嵌入购买路径各环节，而非孤立测试。
insights.action: 梳理自身品类关键购买触点，将感官评价指标与各触点转化数据对齐；关注该活动后续内容，评估引入路径化感官洞察框架的可行性。

insights.title: QSR Evolution Conference
insights.core: Ipsos 发布 QSR Evolution Conference 会议信息，聚焦快餐连锁行业的演进趋势。该活动为行业交流平台，探讨餐饮快消领域的消费者变化与品牌策略，但摘要未披露具体议题或数据。
insights.view: 对 FMCG 感官与 CMI 而言，QSR 是高频、强感官驱动的品类，其行业会议往往反映口味创新、质构偏好与消费场景迁移。虽无细节，但提示我们关注餐饮渠道的感官趋势外溢至零售包装食品的可能。
insights.action: 建议追踪该会议后续发布的议题与演讲内容，尤其涉及消费者口味、质地偏好及体验创新的部分，并评估其对自身品类感官策略与消费者研究的借鉴价值。

insights.title: Ipsos to rank online grocery leaders in 2024 Grocery Ecommerce Experience Report
insights.core: Ipsos将于2024年发布杂货电商体验报告，对在线杂货零售商进行排名，评估其电商体验表现，反映该渠道竞争加剧与消费者体验重要性提升。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，线上杂货渠道的体验排名将影响产品选择、包装感知与购买决策，需关注电商环境下的感官线索（如图片、描述、评价）如何替代线下体验，并纳入消费者洞察框架。
insights.action: 建议追踪该报告排名与指标，结合自身品类分析线上体验痛点，优化产品页面、包装描述与评价管理，并开展电商场景下的感官与消费者研究。

insights.title: Meijer, H-E-B earn top spots in Ipsos’ 2024 Grocery Ecommerce Experience Report
insights.core: Ipsos发布2024年美国杂货电商体验报告，Meijer与H-E-B在消费者体验评选中位居前列，反映零售渠道在电商履约、界面与服务质量上的差异化竞争格局。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，渠道电商体验正成为产品触达与复购的关键变量。不同零售商的平台特性会影响消费者对品类、包装与风味的感知路径，需将渠道体验纳入消费者旅程研究框架。
insights.action: 建议梳理重点零售电商平台的体验维度，结合自身品类开展渠道间消费者感知对比，识别体验短板与机会点，优化线上产品呈现与内容策略。

insights.title: Panda Express, Whataburger, and Chick-Fil-A earn top spots in Ipsos’ 2024 QSR/Fast Casual Restaurant Digital Ordering Performance Study
insights.core: Ipsos发布2024年QSR/快休闲餐厅数字点餐绩效研究，Panda Express、Whataburger和Chick-Fil-A位列前茅。该研究评估了各品牌在数字化点餐体验上的表现，反映快餐行业数字化竞争加剧。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，数字点餐已从便利工具演变为品牌体验的关键触点。点餐流程的流畅度、界面设计与推荐逻辑直接影响消费者预期与复购，需将数字交互纳入整体感官体验研究框架，而非孤立评估。
insights.action: 建议将数字点餐体验纳入消费者旅程地图，重点监测点餐效率、个性化推荐接受度及跨渠道一致性。可对标头部品牌，诊断自身数字触点短板，并测试界面优化对满意度与客单价的拉动。

insights.title: How Jeep is charting a new course for its marketing
insights.core: Jeep正在调整其市场营销策略，重新规划品牌传播路径。文章探讨了该汽车品牌如何在新市场环境下寻找营销方向，但摘要信息有限，未披露具体策略细节。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，这提示品牌需在品类增长放缓或竞争格局变化时主动重构营销叙事。汽车行业面临的品牌差异化、消费者心智争夺与快消品有共通性，值得关注其如何平衡传统品牌资产与新兴消费触达方式。
insights.action: 建议追踪Jeep后续具体举措，提取其品牌重塑框架；同时审视自身品类是否存在类似的品牌老化或传播效率下降信号，提前准备营销策略迭代预案。

insights.title: Campaign Trail: Brooklinen goes in-house for first celebrity-led effort
insights.core: Brooklinen首次推出名人主导营销活动，并选择将相关能力收回内部运作，而非依赖外部代理。这反映出品牌在名人合作策略上更强调自主掌控与品牌一致性。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，名人营销正从单纯流量采买转向品牌资产与消费者感知的深度管理。感官与情感线索需与名人形象统一，避免认知割裂。内部化意味着洞察团队要更早介入创意，提供消费者语言与感官预期依据。
insights.action: 建议梳理名人合作中的感官与情感触点，建立内部快速测试机制，在创意早期验证消费者感知一致性，并沉淀可复用的评估框架。

insights.title: Wayfair ups investment in sports for values-focused brand platform
insights.core: Wayfair加大体育营销投入，将其作为面向价值观驱动型消费者构建品牌平台的核心抓手，通过赞助与内容合作强化品牌认同。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，体育场景正成为价值观营销的高效触点，快消品牌需关注消费者在运动情境下的感官与情绪诉求，将品牌价值主张与具体体验场景绑定，而非泛化传播。
insights.action: 建议梳理目标人群的体育内容消费习惯与价值观标签，测试体育场景下的感官营销素材，建立场景-价值观-产品体验的关联评估框架。

insights.title: M&M’s candy mascots hop genres in ads tapping into film, TV tropes
insights.summary: BBDO Chicago is behind “Screentime,” a campaign that gives crime thrillers, telenovelas and “Survivor” a humorous spin.
insights.core: M&M’s 推出由 BBDO 芝加哥打造的 "Screentime" 广告战役，让品牌糖果角色跨界演绎犯罪惊悚片、拉美肥皂剧和《幸存者》等影视综艺套路，以幽默方式借势流行文化。
insights.view: 对 FMCG 感官与 CMI 而言，这标志着品牌资产正从产品功能转向文化共鸣：M&M’s 用角色人格化承载内容娱乐性，而非单纯强调口味。CMI 需关注消费者对品牌 IP 在非产品场景中的情感联结，感官线索退居次位，叙事与情绪成为记忆锚点。
insights.action: 建议立即测试目标人群对影视梗广告的情绪唤起与品牌回想，评估角色 IP 跨场景延展的接受度；同时监测竞品是否跟进内容化叙事，将感官卖点嵌入娱乐语境以维持差异化。

insights.title: How Tecovas uses music for its Western-focused marketing
insights.core: Tecovas 通过音乐营销强化其西部牛仔品牌定位，将音乐作为连接品牌文化与目标消费者的核心媒介，而非简单广告配乐。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，这提示感官研究不应局限于产品本身，品牌可通过听觉维度构建感官印记。音乐能触发情感联想与身份认同，是低成本高渗透的感官触点，尤其适合有鲜明文化标签的品牌。
insights.action: 建议在品牌感官资产盘点中纳入听觉维度，测试不同音乐风格对品牌联想与购买意愿的影响，建立听觉识别系统并跨渠道一致应用。

insights.title: Costco delivers another strong quarter
insights.summary: Fresh-food comps help drive Q4 sales growth as company defies grocery trends
insights.core: Costco最新季度业绩再度强劲，生鲜品类同店销售成为主要驱动力，在整体杂货零售普遍承压的背景下逆势增长，展现出会员制仓储渠道的独特韧性。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这提示渠道分化加剧：会员制仓储以精选SKU与高性价比建立信任，消费者在生鲜等高频品类更依赖其品质稳定性。感官研究需关注大包装、家庭共享场景下的体验一致性，CMI应重新校准渠道权重与购买动机模型。
insights.action: 建议将Costco等会员制仓储纳入重点渠道样本，追踪生鲜及自有品牌感官表现与复购动因；在消费者研究中增设渠道信任与价值感知维度，指导产品规格与风味策略适配该渠道。

insights.title: Grocery execs may want to pay more attention to GLP-1 use
insights.summary: Not enough are seeing the impact a few years down the line
insights.core: 超市高管对GLP-1（减肥药）使用趋势的长期影响关注不足，未能预见其数年后对食品消费结构、品类需求及购物行为的实质性冲击。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，GLP-1用户可能改变食量、口味偏好和感官满足阈值，传统消费洞察模型若忽略该人群，将误判品类增长与产品开发方向。需将用药状态纳入消费者分层。
insights.action: 立即在消费者追踪中增加GLP-1使用筛查，细分用药人群的感官偏好与购买频次；联合品类团队评估高糖高脂产品的长期风险，并测试适配小份量、高蛋白或强风味的产品概念。

insights.title: Publix sued over alleged E. coli death
insights.summary: Florida man files lawsuit claiming wife died after eating frozen blueberries
insights.core: Publix因一名佛罗里达男子起诉其冷冻蓝莓致其妻感染大肠杆菌死亡而面临法律诉讼，事件直指超市自有品牌冷冻食品的食品安全与供应链管控问题。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，食品安全负面事件会直接冲击消费者对自有品牌的信任与感官预期，尤其冷冻品类的风味与安全感知高度绑定。零售商需重新审视供应商审核与危机沟通策略，避免信任崩塌波及整个品类。
insights.action: 建议立即复盘冷冻果蔬供应链的微生物风险节点，强化供应商审核与追溯体系；同时建立食品安全舆情监测机制，将消费者信任指标纳入CMI常规追踪，提前储备危机沟通话术。

insights.title: Publix’s Florida BOGO is a no go: shoppers
insights.summary: Customers voice their frustration over other states having easier requirements
insights.core: Publix在佛罗里达州的买一送一（BOGO）促销被消费者吐槽，原因是其他州的参与门槛更低，导致佛州购物者感到不公平，引发不满情绪。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，这揭示促销机制的地域差异会直接冲击消费者公平感知与品牌信任。感官研究虽不直接相关，但促销体验属于整体消费体验的一环，不公平感可能迁移至产品评价与复购意愿，需在消费者洞察中纳入促销公平性监测。
insights.action: 建议立即开展跨州消费者公平感知调研，量化BOGO规则差异对满意度、忠诚度的影响；同时评估统一促销门槛或对佛州进行补偿性沟通的可行性，避免负面口碑扩散。

insights.title: Grocery workers are struggling since SNAP cuts
insights.summary: About UsNewsletters AdvertiseWebinarsSubscribeSubscribeGrocery OperationsRelated TopicsGrocery TechnologyLegislation & Regulatory NewsMergers & AcquisitionsInde
insights.core: SNAP福利削减后，美国杂货零售一线员工面临客流与结账压力，同时低收入消费者购买力下降，门店运营与消费行为发生结构性变化。
insights.view: 作为CMI顾问，需关注政策变动对低收入客群购买频次、品类选择及价格敏感度的直接影响，这将在感官偏好测试和产品定位中引入新的价格-价值权衡维度，影响快消品在价值渠道的铺货与沟通策略。
insights.action: 建议立即将SNAP政策变量纳入消费者分群模型，追踪受影响门店的品类销售与员工反馈，调整价值型产品的感官诉求和促销信息，优先保障高敏感客群的核心体验。

insights.title: DoorDash now has a tracking tool
insights.summary: Brand Center combines data from purchases with info collected by Dashers inside stores
insights.core: DoorDash推出Brand Center追踪工具，将消费者购买数据与Dasher在店内采集的信息结合，为品牌提供从货架到交付的全链路数据视图，强化零售媒体与履约数据的整合能力。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，这意味着购物者洞察从问卷与POS向实时履约场景延伸。品牌可获取店内执行与消费场景的关联数据，但需警惕数据代表性偏差，Dasher采集的货架信息或成为感官营销与包装测试的新验证维度。
insights.action: 评估Brand Center数据与现有CMI体系的互补性，优先在包装可见性、货架缺货与冲动购买场景做小范围测试，建立履约数据与感官偏好的关联分析框架。

insights.title: Aldi cuts prices to save shoppers $86M
insights.summary: Nearly one-third of its everyday assortment is priced below last year
insights.core: Aldi宣布下调近三分之一日常商品价格，预计为消费者节省8600万美元，价格低于去年同期水平，反映其在通胀环境下强化低价定位、争夺价格敏感客群的策略。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，价格战升级将压缩品牌溢价空间，消费者对性价比的敏感度上升，感官体验需与价格锚点重新匹配；自有品牌份额或提升，倒逼品牌方在风味、口感等感官差异上建立不可替代性。
insights.action: 建议立即启动价格敏感客群细分研究，测试感官体验与价格带组合的接受度；同步监测Aldi自有品牌动向，调整产品感官定位与沟通策略，避免陷入纯价格竞争。

insights.title: Sam’s Club exec leaks pieces of Thanksgiving meal
insights.summary: It comes from feedback from the retailer’s Member’s Mark group
insights.core: 山姆会员店高管透露了感恩节大餐的组成部分，这些信息源自其自有品牌Member’s Mark团队的反馈。
insights.view: 这表明零售商正利用会员反馈驱动自有品牌节日商品的开发与迭代，对FMCG感官研究而言，意味着需将消费者定性反馈系统化地融入产品概念测试，尤其关注节日场景下的风味与体验预期。
insights.action: 建议立即梳理自有品牌节日产品的会员反馈闭环，建立从CMI洞察到感官规格的快速转化机制，并针对感恩节等关键节点开展前瞻性概念测试。

insights.title: Conagra identifies 3 major trends reshaping America’s $198B snack industry
insights.summary: Bold flavors, functional benefits and permissible indulgence are driving snacking choices as consumers seek more personalized experiences
insights.core: Conagra指出重塑美国1980亿美元零食行业的三大趋势：大胆风味、功能益处与可接受的放纵。消费者追求更个性化的零食体验，推动品类创新方向转变。
insights.view: 对感官研究与CMI而言，这意味需将风味强度、功能感知与罪恶感平衡纳入统一测试框架。个性化要求从人群细分转向个体偏好建模，传统喜好度量表可能失效，需引入情境化与情绪测量。
insights.action: 立即启动三趋势的感官属性映射，建立风味-功能-放纵感联合评价体系；在CMI中增加个性化偏好聚类与情境消费日志，指导产品概念快速筛选。

insights.title: Neighborhood Intelligence reworks Fathom deal
insights.core: Neighborhood Intelligence 对 Fathom 交易进行重新调整，涉及零售媒体与社区数据领域的合作或并购变动。该消息来自 Retail Dive，但摘要仅含图片链接，具体交易细节、金额与条款未在给定信息中披露。
insights.view: 对快消感官研究与 CMI 而言，此类零售数据资产重组提示：社区级、门店级消费数据正被重新整合，未来消费者洞察的颗粒度可能进一步细化到邻里层级，品牌需关注数据源稳定性与可比性变化。
insights.action: 建议追踪该交易后续披露，评估其是否影响现有零售数据合作与消费者面板覆盖；同时梳理自身 CMI 数据供应链，识别对第三方零售数据依赖的风险点并准备替代方案。

insights.title: Target is opening a store in the Hamptons. It’s not red.
insights.summary: The retailer’s signature color is not part of the external facade of the building at its new location in Bridgehampton, New York.
insights.core: Target在纽约Bridgehampton开设新店，外立面未使用其标志性红色，以适配汉普顿高端社区审美。这体现零售商在特定市场放弃统一品牌视觉，转向本地化门店设计策略。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，门店外观是品牌感官资产的核心触点。Target此举说明，在高端或审美敏感市场，标准化视觉可能引发排斥。品牌需评估视觉符号的刚性边界，并研究不同客群对色彩、材质与建筑语言的隐性期待。
insights.action: 建议针对高端社区门店开展视觉偏好测试，量化标志性色彩与本地化设计的接受度差异；建立门店感官资产灵活度分级，明确哪些元素可妥协、哪些必须保留。

insights.title: TJX CEO: Distribution model will help weather El Niño
insights.core: TJX CEO表示其灵活的配送与采购模式有助于应对厄尔尼诺等气候异常带来的需求波动，强调供应链弹性对零售企业稳定运营的价值。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，气候变量正成为影响消费场景与品类需求的关键外部因子。厄尔尼诺可能改变季节性消费节奏与区域偏好，需将气候数据纳入消费者行为追踪与感官偏好波动的解释框架。
insights.action: 建议在CMI监测中引入气候异常指标，按区域和季节拆解品类需求变化；同步评估供应链波动对产品新鲜度、感官体验一致性的潜在影响。

insights.title: The Weekly Closeout: What will happen to Michael Kors and J. Crew celebrates its Barn Jacket
insights.core: 本期零售周报聚焦两大品牌动态：Michael Kors面临被Capri集团出售或战略调整的不确定性，而J.Crew则借复古Barn Jacket外套的流行庆祝其经典单品回归。内容反映时尚零售品牌在资产重组与怀旧营销间的不同路径。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，品牌资产波动直接影响消费者感知与购买信心。Michael Kors的归属悬念可能削弱其轻奢定位的稳定性；J.Crew的Barn Jacket回潮则验证了经典单品通过触感、版型与复古叙事重建情感联结的潜力，提示感官线索在品牌复兴中的杠杆作用。
insights.action: 建议监测Michael Kors品牌健康度与价格敏感度变化，同时拆解J.Crew Barn Jacket的材质、廓形与传播话术，提炼可复用的怀旧感官策略，用于自身经典产品线激活或新品概念测试。

insights.title: Tapestry to sell via Google’s Gemini app, AI Mode
insights.core: Tapestry（Coach、Kate Spade母公司）将在谷歌Gemini应用及AI Mode中直接销售商品，成为首批在生成式AI对话界面内嵌入购物功能的品牌之一。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，这意味着消费者洞察的采集场景正从搜索、电商平台延伸到AI对话界面。品牌需重新定义'货架'概念——AI推荐逻辑将影响产品曝光与选择，感官描述与卖点需适配AI可读的结构化语料。
insights.action: 立即测试品牌在Gemini等AI助手中的呈现方式，梳理产品信息在AI语料中的可发现性；将AI对话渠道纳入消费者旅程地图，评估其对品类选择与品牌认知的潜在影响。

insights.title: Stitch Fix keeps sales expectations in check as it loses active clients
insights.summary: The apparel-box retailer is gaining market share, but the tough consumer backdrop took a toll at the end of its fiscal year, executives said Wednesday.
insights.core: Stitch Fix在失去活跃客户的同时维持保守销售预期：虽在获取市场份额，但财年末端受严峻消费环境拖累，管理层对前景持审慎态度。
insights.view: 对CMI的启示：订阅制服饰盒模式在消费降级期面临留存压力，市场份额增长与客户流失可并存，说明用户获取与留存出现结构性分化。感官研究应关注体验型订阅中产品匹配度与个性化推荐对留存的杠杆作用。
insights.action: 建议立即复盘订阅用户的流失节点与感官/偏好匹配数据，将个性化推荐准确度纳入留存预警指标，并针对价格敏感人群测试降级方案与沟通策略。

insights.title: Halloween spending expected to reach $13.5B
insights.core: 万圣节消费预计达135亿美元，显示节日经济持续升温，消费者在体验型、社交型品类上的支出意愿强劲，为快消品季节性营销提供重要窗口。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，节日场景是情绪驱动型消费的高峰，口味、包装、嗅觉等感官线索与节日氛围强关联，需关注限定款、主题化产品在节庆中的溢价能力与社交传播潜力。
insights.action: 建议提前布局万圣节限定感官概念测试，追踪节日场景下的口味偏好与包装视觉吸引力，结合社媒情绪数据验证主题化产品的消费者共鸣度。

insights.title: Retailers tamp down shadow AI but struggle to oversee agentic sprawl
insights.core: 零售商正收紧对员工私自使用AI工具（影子AI）的管理，但在应对多智能体系统（agentic AI）的规模化扩散时缺乏有效监管手段，治理能力明显滞后。
insights.view: 对FMCG的CMI与感官研究而言，消费者洞察团队常自行接入AI工具做文本挖掘、概念测试与舆情分析，易形成影子AI；一旦智能体跨部门自主运行，数据口径、样本隐私与结论可追溯性将失控，影响洞察可信度。
insights.action: 尽快盘点团队在用的AI工具与数据流向，建立白名单与留痕机制；对智能体应用设定审批与审计节点，明确消费者数据使用边界与责任人。

insights.title: Lowe’s debuts drone delivery pilot with Wing, DoorDash
insights.core: Lowe’s联合Wing与DoorDash试点无人机配送，将大件家装商品纳入即时履约网络，标志着无人机配送从餐饮外卖向更复杂零售场景扩展。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，配送方式正成为产品体验的延伸变量：温控、时效、包装完整性可能影响消费者对品质的感知。无人机场景下，小规格、高时效、强即时满足的品类将获得新的感官竞争维度。
insights.action: 建议在消费者体验研究中纳入履约方式变量，测试无人机配送对产品新鲜度、包装完好度及品牌感知的影响；优先评估高频、小体积、高感官敏感品类的适配性。

insights.title: The Backroom: A status check on Target’s turnaround
insights.summary: Since naming Michael Fiddelke CEO, the retailer has made headway on its recovery with sales and traffic growth despite the bumps along the way.
insights.core: Target在任命Michael Fiddelke为CEO后，转型取得阶段性进展，销售额与客流量实现增长，但过程中仍伴随波动与挑战。该报道对其复苏态势进行了阶段性检视。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官研究与CMI而言，Target的复苏表明客流与销售回暖往往先于品类结构优化。零售商在调整期更依赖消费者洞察驱动选品与自有品牌开发，感官体验与货架沟通成为差异化抓手，值得关注其品类策略变化。
insights.action: 建议追踪Target自有品牌及重点品类的上新与陈列调整，结合客流数据评估感官营销机会；将零售商转型节点纳入渠道洞察节奏，及时捕捉选品偏好迁移信号。

insights.title: Sunday Edition: SNAP
insights.summary: $187.94 is the amount of the average monthly SNAP benefit paid to an individual in FY 2025.
insights.core: Food Safety News报道，2025财年美国SNAP（补充营养援助计划）个人月均补助金额为187.94美元，反映低收入群体食品消费的支付能力基准。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，SNAP额度是价格敏感型消费群体的关键约束。187.94美元/月意味着单餐预算极低，产品定价、包装规格与感官价值主张需匹配该人群的性价比诉求，同时关注营养安全与合规沟通。
insights.action: 建议针对SNAP受众开展价格弹性与感官偏好测试，优化小规格、高饱腹感产品组合；在CMI中纳入补助周期对购买行为的影响追踪，并评估政策变动对品类需求的传导。

insights.title: Ravioli recalled because of undeclared lobster
insights.summary: Deano’s Pasta of Somerville, MA, is recalling 20 pounds of Pear and Pecorino Triangoli Ravioli, because it may contain undeclared Lobster. People wh
insights.core: 马萨诸塞州Deano's Pasta召回20磅Pear and Pecorino Triangoli Ravioli，原因是产品可能含有未申报的龙虾成分，构成未标识过敏原风险。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这是过敏原标识与配方交叉污染的典型警示。龙虾属主要过敏原，未申报会触发监管召回并严重损害品牌信任。感官研究需关注多品类共线生产的交叉污染风险，CMI应监测消费者对过敏原标签的信任度与召回事件的舆情反应。
insights.action: 立即核查共线生产的过敏原隔离与清洁验证流程；在感官与标签审核中增加过敏原交叉检查；建立召回舆情监测机制，评估消费者信任影响并准备沟通预案。

insights.title: Cinnamon recalled because of excessive lead levels
insights.summary: Galil Importing Corp. of Hauppauge, NY, is recalling Lior Cinnamon Ground Seasoning because it has the potential to be contaminated with elevated levels of lead
insights.core: 纽约Galil Importing公司因铅含量超标召回Lior肉桂粉调味料，属食品安全合规事件，涉及香料类产品的重金属污染风险。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，铅超标不仅是合规问题，更会触发消费者对风味原料安全性的信任危机；香料类原料的产地、加工与检测链条需纳入感官品质与风险感知的双重评估。
insights.action: 立即排查自身香料供应链的铅等重金属检测记录，强化供应商审核；在消费者沟通中主动透明化原料安全标准，避免风味创新因安全事件被拖累。

insights.title: Frozen sausage recalled after complaints of plastic in product
insights.summary: Fontanini Foods LLC of McCook, IL, is recalling 2,320 pounds of raw, frozen pork breakfast sausage products that may be contaminated with foreign material,
insights.core: Fontanini Foods因产品可能混入塑料异物，召回2,320磅生冷冻猪肉早餐香肠。事件属物理性食品安全风险，涉及冷冻肉制品品类，由投诉触发召回。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，异物投诉是消费者最易感知、传播最快的质量信号，直接冲击品牌信任。冷冻肉制品供应链长、加工环节多，异物风险点隐蔽，需将感官评价前置到原料与生产端，并建立投诉快速归因机制。
insights.action: 立即排查同批次原料与产线异物防控点；将消费者投诉文本纳入CMI监测，识别异味、口感异常等早期信号；对召回批次做感官复检并更新HACCP计划。

insights.title: Chicken stew from Korea recalled because of inspection problem
insights.summary: Sempio Food Services Inc. of Cerritos, CA, is recalling 4,596 pounds of ready-to-eat chicken stew products that were imported from the Republic of Korea without
insights.core: 韩国进口的即食炖鸡产品因检验问题被美国召回，涉及约4596磅产品，由加州Sempio Food Services公司发起，问题指向进口环节未通过合规检验。
insights.view: 对FMCG及感官研究而言，这再次凸显跨境食品合规风险：进口检验问题往往与标签、成分或工艺标准差异相关，直接影响消费者信任与品牌声誉。CMI需关注召回事件对品类感知的溢出效应。
insights.action: 建议排查自身进口产品的检验合规链路，建立召回预警与快速响应机制；同时监测该事件在目标市场的消费者情绪，评估对韩式即食品类及自有品牌的潜在影响。

insights.title: New E. coli outbreak linked to raw milk cheese
insights.summary: More than half of the patients are younger than 5
insights.core: 美国再现与生乳奶酪相关的大肠杆菌疫情，患者中过半为5岁以下儿童，属高风险食源性致病事件，涉及婴幼儿等敏感人群，凸显生鲜乳制品未经巴氏杀菌的微生物安全隐患。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，此类事件会迅速放大消费者对‘天然/生鲜’宣称的风险感知，尤其影响母婴及儿童食品品类。感官研究需关注安全事件后风味与‘新鲜’联想的变化，CMI应追踪信任度与购买意愿的短期波动。
insights.action: 立即监测母婴及乳制品品类的消费者情绪与信任指标，评估‘生鲜/未杀菌’宣称的舆情风险；在感官测试中加入安全感知维度，并为相关产品准备沟通与配方调整预案。

insights.title: UK patient count in Salmonella outbreak passes 600
insights.summary: The FSA is also seeking views on revised listeriosis guidance
insights.core: 英国沙门氏菌疫情患者数突破600人，英国食品标准局（FSA）同时就修订后的李斯特菌防控指南公开征求意见。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，食品安全事件正从合规议题转向消费者信任与风险感知议题。疫情规模扩大将强化消费者对即食、冷链及低加工品类的安全敏感度，感官评价需纳入风险沟通维度。
insights.action: 立即排查涉事供应链，复核李斯特菌与沙门氏菌防控SOP；同步监测消费者信任与购买意愿变化，将安全感知纳入感官测试与舆情追踪指标。

insights.title: Expired eggs used in meal linked to Salmonella outbreak
insights.summary: At least 250 people have fallen sick at a school in the Czech Republic after eating in the cafeteria.The Prague Public Health Authority said the use of eggs pas
insights.core: 捷克一所学校食堂因使用过期鸡蛋引发沙门氏菌疫情，至少250人患病，布拉格公共卫生当局已介入调查。事件暴露了餐饮供应链中食材保质期管理与食品安全监管的严重漏洞。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，食品安全事件会显著影响消费者对品类与渠道的信任，尤其涉及学校等敏感场景。过期原料的使用提示供应链末端执行风险，可能引发对即食、团餐及蛋制品品类的负面感知，需关注信任修复与风险沟通。
insights.action: 建议立即排查相关品类供应链的保质期管控与追溯机制，评估事件对消费者信任度的潜在冲击；针对学校、团餐等场景加强感官与安全双重检测，并准备透明的危机沟通话术，以维护品牌信誉。

insights.title: Salmonella outbreak traced to sprouts spreads to 2 more states
insights.summary: Ten people have been added to the patient count in a Salmonella Bovismorbificans outbreak from recalled broccoli sprouts traced to Evergreen Fresh Sprouts LLC.A
insights.core: 美国Evergreen Fresh Sprouts LLC召回的西兰花芽菜引发鼠伤寒沙门氏菌疫情，病例再增10人并扩散至另外两个州，属典型生鲜供应链微生物污染事件。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，此类食安事件会迅速重塑消费者对生鲜品类的风险感知与信任阈值，进而影响其风味接受度、复购意愿及对'新鲜'标签的解读，需在感官测试中同步监测安全焦虑对偏好数据的干扰。
insights.action: 建议将食安风险感知纳入消费者追踪问卷，结合召回事件窗口做快照调研，识别信任受损品类与人群，并评估其对相关风味宣称与包装信息接受度的短期冲击。

insights.title: Rare E. coli type behind large outbreak in Japan
insights.summary: Researchers in Japan have been unable to pinpoint the contamination route of a large outbreak that sickened more than 170 people.In June 2022, 171 of 934 people
insights.core: 日本2022年6月发生一起涉及171人、波及934人的大肠杆菌疫情，研究人员至今未能确定污染路径，暴露了食源性疾病溯源在供应链复杂场景下的现实困难。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，此类事件提示消费者对食品安全的信任高度依赖可追溯性与透明度；即便污染路径未明，品牌也需通过感官品质稳定性和供应链信息披露来管理风险感知，避免信任危机外溢至品类。
insights.action: 建议将食安溯源能力纳入供应商审核与风险监测体系，并在消费者研究中增加对溯源信息、召回响应与品牌信任的敏感度测试，提前储备沟通预案。

insights.title: Potential infant formula illnesses probed in the UK
insights.summary: Plus a round-up of other incidents involving the FSA
insights.core: 英国食品安全局正调查疑似婴儿配方奶粉引发的疾病事件，并汇总了其他相关食品安全事件。事件涉及婴幼儿这一高敏感人群，指向配方食品安全风险与监管响应。
insights.view: 婴幼儿配方属高信任门槛品类，感官与安全感知高度绑定。此类事件会迅速放大消费者对风味异常、质地变化等感官信号的警觉，CMI需将安全舆情纳入感官风险监测，警惕负面感知向品牌整体信任迁移。
insights.action: 立即排查涉事批次与供应链，建立婴幼儿配方感官异常与安全舆情的联动监测机制，准备消费者沟通口径，并针对家长群体开展信任修复型洞察调研。

insights.title: FDA identifies two new outbreaks
insights.summary: Sources of pathogens have not been identified
insights.core: FDA通报两起新的食源性疾病暴发事件，但致病病原体的来源尚未查明。这意味着监管机构已启动调查，但溯源工作仍处于早期阶段，风险源头不明，可能涉及多品类、多环节的供应链。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，来源不明的暴发会放大消费者对品类安全的不确定感，进而影响风味偏好与购买信心。即便非直接涉事品类，也可能因关联联想被波及，需警惕负面情绪向感官期待迁移。
insights.action: 立即排查自身供应链与在售品类的风险敞口，同步监测社交舆情中消费者对风味、原料安全的情绪变化；预备感官替代方案与透明沟通话术，避免被动响应。

insights.title: Consent decree bans distributor from operating because of rodent infestation, other filth
insights.summary: A consent decree filed in a federal court in Minnesota bars Gold Star Distribution Inc. from distributing food because of persistent insanitary conditions.The c
insights.core: 美国明尼苏达州联邦法院对Gold Star Distribution Inc.下达同意令，因其持续存在鼠患及其他卫生问题，禁止其继续从事食品分销业务。该案例显示监管机构对供应链卫生违规采取零容忍的司法强制措施。
insights.view: 对FMCG与电子烟行业而言，供应链卫生合规是品牌声誉与产品安全的底线。感官研究与CMI需关注分销环节的储存环境对产品风味、气溶胶品质的潜在影响，消费者对异物、污染事件的容忍度极低，一次违规即可引发信任崩塌。
insights.action: 立即审查自身及第三方物流的虫害防治与卫生审计记录，将分销合规纳入供应商准入与年度审核指标；建立消费者投诉中异物/异味信号的快速溯源机制，并准备危机沟通预案。

insights.title: Study findings challenge Campylobacter coli knowledge
insights.summary: Detection of the same type of Campylobacter in several countries has challenged previous beliefs that it is associated with unrelated infections.Researchers rep
insights.core: 研究在多个国家检出同型弯曲杆菌，挑战了此前认为其仅与不相关感染有关的认知，提示该菌可能存在跨国传播或共同污染源，食品安全风险认知需更新。
insights.view: 对快消品感官与CMI而言，微生物风险会直接影响产品风味稳定性与消费者信任。若弯曲杆菌污染具有跨国共性，企业需重新评估供应链与原料风险，并在感官测试中纳入安全关联指标。
insights.action: 建议立即复核相关原料与供应链的微生物监测数据，将弯曲杆菌纳入风险预警清单，并在消费者洞察中追踪安全事件对品类信任与购买意愿的影响。

insights.title: Sprouting seeds recalled because of link to outbreak
insights.summary: Berlin Seeds, of Millersburg, OH, is recalling 950 pounds of alfalfa sprouting seed because the seed has the potential to be contaminated with Shiga toxin-produ
insights.core: 俄亥俄州Berlin Seeds召回950磅苜蓿芽种子，因其可能受志贺毒素污染，与疫情相关联。这是食品安全事件，涉及供应链源头风险。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，此类召回事件提醒我们：食品安全是消费者信任的底线，感官研究需关注污染对产品风味、质地的影响，CMI应监测消费者对品牌安全感知的波动，尤其在生鲜品类。
insights.action: 立即排查自身供应链中类似种子或原料风险，加强供应商审核与检测；CMI团队应启动消费者安全感知追踪，评估事件对品类购买意愿的潜在影响。

insights.title: Don’t toss cannabis leaves: They may contain rare compounds with medical potential
insights.summary: Scientists discovered rare flavoalkaloids in Cannabis leaves for the first time, along with dozens of other phenolic compounds that had never been reported in t
insights.core: 科学家首次在大麻叶片中发现稀有黄酮生物碱及数十种此前未报道的酚类化合物，提示长期被当作废弃物丢弃的叶片可能具备药用开发价值，颠覆了以花部为核心的原料利用逻辑。
insights.view: 对感官与CMI而言，这意味着风味与功能原料的边界正在从传统可食部位向副产物延伸。黄酮生物碱兼具苦味、涩感与潜在生理活性，可能成为新型功能性风味模块；消费者对‘零废弃’‘全株利用’的可持续叙事接受度，也将影响产品概念测试与宣称策略。
insights.action: 建议立即梳理现有植物原料的副产物清单，优先评估叶片类提取物的感官轮廓与法规可行性；同步在CMI中增设‘全株利用/零废弃’概念测试，为后续功能性雾化或食品饮料新品储备原料与故事资产。

insights.title: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
insights.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia. Lab
insights.core: 一项大型健康记录分析显示，氨基葡萄糖使用与轻度认知障碍向痴呆进展的可能性升高25%相关，提示这一流行关节补充剂可能存在认知风险信号。
insights.view: 对FMCG与CMI而言，这再次说明功能性补充剂宣称需以长期安全证据为底线；感官与消费者研究应把认知风险纳入产品概念测试与人群细分，避免仅凭关节健康卖点放大信任。
insights.action: 建议梳理含氨基葡萄糖产品线，复核标签与宣称，补充认知安全文献监测；在CMI问卷中加入长期使用与认知担忧题项，为配方或沟通调整提供依据。

insights.title: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
insights.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begi
insights.core: 科学家发现REM睡眠期间大脑存在能量悖论：尽管脑血流供应增加，但大脑能量似乎仍被梦境消耗，提示供能提升未必等于能量净盈余。
insights.view: 对感官与CMI研究者而言，这提示消费者主观状态（如疲惫、清醒度）不能仅由生理供能指标推断。感官测试与消费者调研若忽视睡眠、情绪等状态变量，可能误读偏好与反应数据，需将生理状态纳入个体差异分层。
insights.action: 在感官与消费者测试中增加睡眠质量、时段与疲劳度筛查，将REM相关状态作为协变量记录；对关键结论做状态分层复核，避免把状态波动误判为产品差异。

insights.title: When what you see doesn’t make sense, your brain does something remarkable
insights.summary: The brain may have a built-in way to quickly settle disagreements between regions processing the same scene. Researchers found that matching signals between two
insights.core: 大脑在视觉信息出现矛盾时，可能具备内置机制快速协调不同脑区的信号，使同一场景的感知达成一致，而非陷入混乱。
insights.view: 对感官研究与CMI而言，这提示消费者对产品外观、包装、口味等跨模态线索不一致时，大脑会自动‘纠偏’，可能掩盖真实体验。品牌若依赖单一感官测试，或低估多感官冲突对偏好的影响。
insights.action: 在感官测试中主动制造并测量跨模态线索冲突（如包装颜色与口味预期不符），观察大脑纠偏如何影响喜好与记忆，据此优化产品一致性设计。

insights.title: Rare pregnancy infections may triple the risk of autism
insights.summary: A major Swedish study of 3.7 million people has found that rare TORCH infections passed from a pregnant woman to the fetus are linked to much higher risks of au
insights.core: 瑞典一项覆盖370万人研究显示，孕期罕见的TORCH母婴感染与子代自闭症风险显著升高（最高约三倍）相关，提示母体感染是神经发育障碍的重要风险因素。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，此洞察强化了‘早期生命暴露影响感官与认知发展’的假设，提示未来消费者偏好、感官敏感度差异可能部分源于围产期健康史，值得在人群分层与感官测试中纳入健康背景变量。
insights.action: 在感官与消费者研究中增设孕期感染/健康史问卷变量，探索其与味觉偏好、质构接受度的关联；同时关注母婴健康类产品的宣称与沟通机会。

insights.title: NAW to appeal ruling that upheld Oregon EPR law
insights.core: 美国全国酿酒商协会（NAW）宣布将就俄勒冈州生产者责任延伸（EPR）法案的维持原判裁决提起上诉，该法案要求包装生产商承担回收成本与责任。
insights.view: 对快消品CMI与感官研究而言，EPR合规将重塑包装策略，进而影响产品触感、开启体验与货架感知。包装材质与结构受限可能改变消费者感官预期，需提前评估合规包装对品牌感知的潜在影响。
insights.action: 立即梳理俄勒冈及其他EPR推进州的产品包装清单，联合研发与法规团队评估替代包装的感官与成本影响，并启动消费者对可持续包装接受度的快速定性测试。

insights.title: Nestlé breaks down its path to 2030 for virgin plastic reduction
insights.core: 雀巢公布其到2030年减少原生塑料使用的路径规划，披露阶段性目标与包装设计、再生材料、循环模式等具体举措，展现大型FMCG企业在塑料减量上的系统化推进思路。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，包装材质变更会直接影响产品外观、触感、开合体验乃至气味阻隔，进而改变消费者感知与接受度。塑料减量不是纯可持续议题，而是需要纳入感官与消费者测试的包装创新变量。
insights.action: 建议将包装可持续改造纳入感官与消费者测试流程，针对再生材料、减薄瓶身、替换结构开展触感、开合、保鲜与货架辨识度对比测试，提前识别体验风险与沟通机会点。

insights.title: ProAmpac comes in hot with grab-and-go wings box
insights.summary: The supplier designed and produced a unique hot box for Flamin’ Hot chicken wings in Circle K stores. Hot-hold solutions are outpacing demand
insights.core: ProAmpac为Circle K便利店设计并生产了一款用于Flamin' Hot鸡翅的保温包装盒，主打即取即食的热食场景。文章指出，保温包装解决方案的需求增速已超过市场实际需求，成为包装供应商争夺的新赛道。
insights.view: 热食即取场景正在从餐饮向便利店零售迁移，这对感官研究提出新命题：保温包装不仅是功能载体，更直接影响消费者对温度、香气释放和第一口风味的感知。CMI需将包装纳入感官体验链路，而非仅作为物流变量。
insights.action: 建议在便利店热食品类测试中增加包装变量，对比保温盒与普通包装对风味感知、复购意愿的影响；同时监测Circle K等渠道的热食SKU扩张节奏，评估自身品类的切入机会。

insights.title: Aldi to roll out first ready-made meals line
insights.core: Aldi将推出其首个即食餐（ready-made meals）产品线，标志着这家以自有品牌和低价著称的折扣零售商进一步向预制/即食食品领域扩张，试图以高性价比切入日常用餐场景。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，折扣渠道加码即食餐意味着价格敏感型消费者的味觉期待被重新校准：他们要求接近餐饮级的风味与质地，却只愿付零售价。感官基准需覆盖竞品与餐饮外卖双重参照，消费者测试应关注饱腹感、复热后口感衰减及清洁标签容忍度。
insights.action: 建议立即建立即食餐品类感官与消费者测试框架，重点测评复热稳定性、风味强度与质构；同步监测Aldi上市后的价格带与口味组合，为自有品牌对标或差异化提供依据。

insights.title: Leftovers: Hidden Valley Ranch goes dark for Halloween | V8 energizes with electrolytes
insights.core: Food Dive报道两则快消动态：Hidden Valley Ranch借万圣节推出暗黑主题限定产品，V8则推出含电解质的能量型新品。两者均属品牌通过季节性/功能性概念延伸产品线，以激活消费者尝鲜与场景关联。
insights.view: 从感官与CMI角度看，万圣节限定依赖视觉与包装的‘暗黑’感官冲击制造话题，而V8加电解质则切入功能饮料的清爽/能量感官诉求。品牌正用限定口味与功能叠加测试消费者对风味与质地的接受边界，是低成本的感官概念验证。
insights.action: 建议追踪两新品在社媒的感官评价与复购信号，尤其限定款的视觉-味觉一致性。若自身品类有节庆或功能化机会，可快速小批量测试类似概念，收集消费者对风味、包装与场景联想的反馈。

insights.title: Why food rating apps can miss the mark on nutrition
insights.core: 文章探讨食品评分类App为何常在营养评估上失准：这类工具多依赖简化算法或有限数据，难以反映真实营养构成，可能误导消费者判断，也削弱品牌在健康定位上的沟通可信度。
insights.view: 对感官研究与CMI而言，这提示消费者对‘健康’的判断正被第三方评分中介化。若评分逻辑与产品真实感官体验、配方事实脱节，品牌将失去叙事主导权。研究需同时追踪评分认知与实际营养感知的落差。
insights.action: 建议立即梳理主流评分App对本品类的打分逻辑与偏差，将评分影响纳入消费者洞察框架；同步用感官测试校准‘健康感’沟通，避免被外部评分定义。

insights.title: Grocery inflation is primed to rise
insights.core: 该报道指出，美国食品杂货通胀预计将再度抬头。虽未提供具体数据，但方向性判断明确：此前相对回落的食品价格压力可能重新上行，成本端压力正从上游向下游零售价格传导。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，通胀回升意味着消费者价格敏感度上升，会加速向自有品牌与性价比产品迁移，并抬高对口味、质地等感官体验的容忍门槛。感官研究需重新校准‘物有所值’的体验基准，避免配方降本损害核心感官记忆点。
insights.action: 建议立即复盘核心品类的价格弹性与感官属性优先级，识别可降本但不伤及关键感官指标的环节；同步监测消费者价格感知与转换行为，为可能的配方或规格调整预留测试窗口。

insights.title: How ready-to-drink cocktails are reshaping the spirits industry
insights.core: 文章探讨即饮鸡尾酒（RTD）如何重塑烈酒行业，指出其以便捷、多元风味和年轻化定位，正在改变传统烈酒的消费场景与竞争格局，推动品牌加速产品创新与渠道调整。
insights.view: 对感官研究与CMI而言，RTD的爆发意味着评价体系需从纯饮体验转向混合风味、甜度、气泡感与余味的综合平衡；消费者洞察应关注饮用场景碎片化、低度化偏好及跨品类替代，传统烈酒感官标准面临重构。
insights.action: 建议立即开展RTD风味图谱与竞品感官基准测试，建立场景化消费者测试框架，追踪年轻群体对甜度、酒精感与风味的接受阈值，为产品迭代与定位提供数据支撑。

insights.title: General Mills prioritizes innovation following recent price cuts
insights.core: 通用磨坊在近期降价后，将战略重心转向创新，表明其试图以产品差异化而非单纯价格竞争来重获增长动力，反映了当前食品行业价格战后的策略回调。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，这意味着企业需重新评估降价对消费者感知与品牌价值的侵蚀，并将研究前置到创新概念筛选与感官宣称验证，以支撑溢价回归。
insights.action: 建议立即启动消费者价格敏感度与感官偏好联合研究，识别可支撑创新溢价的关键感官属性，并建立创新概念快速测试机制。

insights.title: Surfside drops trade dress lawsuit against Anheuser-Busch
insights.core: Surfside撤销对百威英博的包装外观（trade dress）诉讼，具体和解条款未披露。该案原涉及即饮鸡尾酒品类中品牌视觉标识的模仿争议，反映出新兴品牌与酒业巨头在货架视觉资产上的摩擦。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，此案提示货架视觉识别（颜色、字体、瓶型、图案）是快消品差异化与法律风险的交叉点。新兴品牌常借视觉趋同快速获客，但若缺乏系统性包装资产审计，易陷入诉讼或被迫改版，进而冲击消费者辨识与复购。
insights.action: 建议立即梳理自身核心SKU的包装视觉资产，建立与竞品的货架辨识度基线；在新品开发流程中加入包装显著性测试与法律预审，避免视觉趋同带来的合规与品牌稀释风险。

insights.title: SA ready-meal business expands access for SaH, NDIS shoppers
insights.summary: Customers can shop at the company’s stores in Malvern, Parkside, Glenelg, Port Elliot and Modbury. The post SA ready-meal business expands access for SaH, NDIS
insights.core: 南澳一家即食餐企业将其门店网络扩展至Malvern、Parkside、Glenelg、Port Elliot和Modbury，为SaH（居家支持）与NDIS（残障保险计划）消费者提供更便捷的购买渠道，属于渠道与服务可及性扩张。
insights.view: 该案例显示即食餐正从零售货架向照护与残障福利支付体系渗透，购买决策者与食用者分离，感官与CMI研究需纳入护理协调员、家属及支付方等间接用户，并关注质地、营养标识与份量等非风味维度。
insights.action: 建议针对NDIS/SaH场景建立细分用户画像，测试适老适障质地与包装易用性，并跟踪福利支付政策对渠道选择与复购的影响。

insights.title: MooGoo partners with The Wiggles for kids’ oral care campaign
insights.summary: The launch introduces four distinct flavours: Strawberries & Cream, Vanilla Ice Cream, Watermelon Sherbet, and Blueberry Smoothie. The post MooGoo partners with
insights.core: MooGoo与儿童娱乐IP The Wiggles合作推出儿童口腔护理 campaign，一次上市四款甜品风味：草莓奶油、香草冰淇淋、西瓜雪葩和蓝莓冰沙，将口腔护理与儿童熟悉的甜品味觉绑定。
insights.view: 这是典型的‘风味桥接’策略：用甜品风味降低儿童对刷牙的抗拒，把感官愉悦前置到功能品类。对CMI而言，儿童品类的风味偏好高度依赖IP信任与家长感知安全性，风味命名需同时打动孩子与家长，且要规避‘可吞咽甜味’的合规与认知风险。
insights.action: 建议立即开展儿童与家长双视角的风味概念测试，验证四款风味的偏好排序与‘甜而不腻’的感知边界；同步评估IP联名对购买意愿的增量，并监测是否引发误食联想，为后续风味延展与合规沟通定调。

insights.title: Finder reveals 16.1 million Aussies affected by shrinkflation
insights.summary: “In some cases, it's even worse than that – the product gets smaller and the price goes up at the same time.” The post Finder reveals 16.1 million Aussies affec
insights.core: Finder调查显示，澳大利亚约1610万消费者受‘缩水式通胀’影响，即产品分量减少而价格不变甚至上涨，部分案例中产品变小与涨价同时发生。
insights.view: 对CMI与感官研究而言，缩水式通胀不仅是价格议题，更直接冲击产品体验：克重、口数、风味释放等感官指标随规格变化而改变，易引发消费者察觉与信任流失，需将规格变动纳入感官与消费者追踪体系。
insights.action: 建议立即建立规格与价格变动的监测台账，针对主力SKU开展盲测与消费者感知追踪，评估缩水对口感、满足感及复购意愿的影响，并据此优化沟通或产品策略。

insights.title: Noosa-based CocoCoast targets $200m annual revenue, plots US return
insights.summary: Co-founder Damian Russell calls the company’s five-year ambition “a substantial increase” from where it is today. The post Noosa-based CocoCoast targets $200m a
insights.core: 澳大利亚Noosa品牌CocoCoast公布五年目标，计划实现年营收2亿美元，并重新进入美国市场；联合创始人称这是相较当前规模的显著跃升。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI团队而言，这意味着又一家区域健康饮品品牌进入规模化与跨国扩张阶段；美国回归将面临口味偏好、甜度感知与标签期望差异，需以本地化感官测试与消费者细分支撑定位，而非简单复制本土配方。
insights.action: 建议立即建立美国目标人群的品类口味基准与竞品感官图谱，开展跨文化甜度、质地与风味接受度测试，并将结果嵌入产品调整与上市沟通策略。

insights.title: Saputo Dairy Australia launches high-protein long-life milks
insights.summary: Each product contains 15 grams of protein per 300ml serving. The post Saputo Dairy Australia launches high-protein long-life milks appeared first on Inside FMCG
insights.core: Saputo Dairy Australia推出高蛋白常温长效奶，每300毫升含15克蛋白质。这反映乳企正通过高蛋白功能化与常温长保质期技术，切入健康化与便利化消费场景。
insights.view: 对感官与CMI而言，高蛋白常伴随质地、口感与风味缺陷，需重点评估蛋白来源与体系稳定性对感官体验的影响；同时常温长保意味着货架期感官衰减与消费者接受度需跨时间验证，不能仅依赖即时测试。
insights.action: 建议立即开展竞品感官基准测试，聚焦蛋白含量、口感顺滑度与后味；并设计加速货架期感官追踪，结合消费者使用场景验证常温高蛋白奶的复购驱动因素。

insights.title: Romeo’s Foodland Royal Park wins IGA international retail award
insights.summary: The Royal Park store was opened in May 2023. The post Romeo’s Foodland Royal Park wins IGA international retail award appeared first on Inside FMCG.
insights.core: Romeo’s Foodland Royal Park门店于2023年5月开业，荣获IGA国际零售奖，体现其在食品零售运营与门店体验上的国际认可。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，该奖项提示零售终端体验、品类陈列与门店服务正成为品牌差异化的关键触点；独立零售商通过体验创新可建立消费者忠诚，值得作为渠道洞察样本。
insights.action: 建议将该门店作为零售体验标杆案例，拆解其感官营销、动线设计与品类组合策略，并纳入渠道走访或消费者拦截研究计划。

insights.title: How researchers are building a more resilient food future
insights.summary: RMIT researchers are tackling the questions shaping what Australia grows, makes and eats. The post How researchers are building a more resilient food future app
insights.core: RMIT研究人员正围绕澳大利亚农业种植、食品制造与消费结构的关键问题展开研究，目标是构建更具韧性的食品未来，涉及从生产端到餐桌的系统性议题。
insights.view: 对FMCG感官与CMI而言，食品韧性议题将重塑原料可得性、配方稳定性与消费者偏好。供应链波动会直接影响产品感官一致性和价格敏感度，需将外部环境变量纳入感官与消费者测试框架。
insights.action: 建议梳理自身品类对气候与供应链的暴露度，在消费者研究中加入韧性相关态度与支付意愿题项，并与上游原料研究机构建立信息联动。

insights.title: Seedlab expands support for small businesses as retail pressures mount
insights.summary: Seedlab MD Kenna MacTavish said support for small businesses needs to go beyond helping them secure shelf space. The post Seedlab expands support for small busi
insights.core: Seedlab 扩大对小型企业的支持，其董事总经理 Kenna MacTavish 指出，零售压力加剧下，支持不能止于帮助小企业获得货架空间，还需覆盖更广泛的零售能力建设。
insights.view: 对 FMCG 感官与 CMI 而言，这意味着渠道研究需从‘上架’转向‘动销’。小企业缺乏消费者洞察与感官验证资源，若仅给货架，转化率与复购仍难保障，CMI 应把货架表现与感官接受度、复购数据打通评估。
insights.action: 建议将感官测试与消费者洞察打包为小企业可负担的轻量模块，优先验证核心 SKU 的接受度与货架转化，再据此优化选品与陈列，避免盲目铺货。

insights.title: Peters Ice Cream pairs Maxibon and Barney Banana for limited-edition release
insights.summary: The Maxibon Barney Banana features a banana-flavoured ice cream centre split between two serving styles. The post Peters Ice Cream pairs Maxibon and Barney Bana
insights.core: Peters Ice Cream将旗下Maxibon与Barney Banana两个品牌联名，推出限量版香蕉风味冰淇淋，产品中心为香蕉味冰淇淋，并采用两种食用形态。这是典型的品牌跨界与怀旧风味结合的限量新品。
insights.view: 对感官研究与CMI而言，此案例凸显‘品牌资产+风味记忆’的联名逻辑：香蕉风味自带童年怀旧联想，双形态设计则创造质地与吃法的感官差异点。限量策略可用于低成本测试风味接受度与联名溢价，为后续常规化提供消费者反馈依据。
insights.action: 建议在上市期同步开展感官偏好与概念接受度测试，重点捕捉香蕉风味强度、双形态的食用场景偏好及联名溢价支付意愿；对比历史限量款数据，判断是否具备转为常规SKU或延展联名矩阵的潜力。

insights.title: PepsiCo brings portfolio together with House of Brands campaign
insights.summary: Only 18 per cent of consumers associate the company with brands beyond Pepsi. The post PepsiCo brings portfolio together with House of Brands campaign appeared
insights.core: 百事公司发起‘品牌之家’营销战役，旨在强化消费者对其旗下多元品牌的认知。数据显示仅18%的消费者能将百事与百事以外的品牌关联，暴露出集团品牌资产过度集中于主品牌、子品牌认知严重不足的问题。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，这揭示了集团品牌架构中‘主品牌光环’与‘子品牌独立性’的张力。感官研究需注意：消费者对子品牌的感官预期可能被主品牌形象扭曲，需独立测量各品牌感官印记。品牌联想度低意味着跨品类风味延伸与创新接受度存在隐性壁垒。
insights.action: 建议开展子品牌感官资产与品牌联想的联合诊断，识别哪些品牌可通过感官线索强化与母品牌的正向关联，哪些需保持独立以避免认知混淆。优先测试‘品牌之家’ campaign 对子品牌无提示认知与购买意愿的拉动效果。

insights.title: Endeavour leverages sales data for Dan Murphy’s and BWS
insights.summary: The new platform will connect Endeavour’s trade partners to retail insights gathered from over 1700 stores. The post Endeavour leverages sales data for Dan Murp
insights.core: Endeavour集团推出新平台，将1700多家Dan Murphy’s和BWS门店的零售数据开放给贸易伙伴，帮助其获取销售洞察。
insights.view: 对CMI而言，零售商数据开放意味着品牌可更精准追踪终端动销与消费者选择，但感官研究需与真实购买数据结合，才能验证风味偏好与复购驱动。数据颗粒度提升将推动感官指标与销售指标联动分析。
insights.action: 建议品牌方主动接入该平台，将感官测试结果与门店销售数据做关联建模，识别高转化风味特征，并调整产品组合与陈列策略。

readings.title: Trump’s “Most EXCLUSIVE DINNER IN THE WORLD”
body: Politics / Donald Trump / The Logoff Trump’s “Most EXCLUSIVE DINNER IN THE WORLD” The latest way Trump is using crypto to profit off of the presidency. by Cameron Peters Oct 1, 2026, 10:30 PM UTC Gift Donald Trump waves to the media on the South Lawn of the White House on September 26, 2026. Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images Cameron Peters is a staff editor at Vox. This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here . Welcome to The Logoff: Donald Trump is once again selling access to the highest bidder(s). What’s happening? On Thursday, the Washington Sun’s Jeff Stein reported that Trump will reprise his 2025 “crypto dinner” later this year, hosting some of the top investors in the $TRUMP memecoin at his Virginia golf club. The top 185 holders of $TRUMP will receive an invite to the event, which the website describes as the “Most EXCLUSIVE DINNER IN THE WORLD.” The top 29 $TRUMP holders will also be eligible for a “special VIP reception.” What is $TRUMP? As my colleague Adam Clark Estes explained last year , memecoins like $TRUMP are “all but make-believe.” The coin is a crypto token, or “a type of digital asset that’s built on a cryptocurrency’s blockchain, but it is not a full featured cryptocurrency, like bitcoin.” In other words, buying it doesn’t get you very much — the value of the coin has collapsed since early last year when Trump took office — but it will get you a chance to have dinner with the president. What’s the context? This will be the third major event Trump has hosted for buyers of $TRUMP, following a May 2025 dinner at his Virginia club and a “crypto and business conference” earlier this year at Mar-a-Lago , where Trump gave a keynote speech. But it’s just one of the many, many ways that Trump and his family have found to enrich themselves through crypto: There’s also another memecoin, $MELANIA, and his lucrative crypto firm, World Liberty Financial, which received a $500 million investment from a member of the United Arab Emirates royal family last year. Strictly speaking, as Stein points out, Trump himself does not own the company minting $TRUMP, though he still profits handsomely , to the tune of $636 million last year, from transaction fees and other revenue. And he’s made even more off World Liberty Financial, which he and his sons do own, along with others: $799 million in 2025 alone, according to financial disclosure forms filed earlier this year. ##段落
政治 / 唐纳德·特朗普 / The Logoff 特朗普的“全球最独家晚宴” 特朗普利用加密货币从总统职位中获利的最新方式。 作者：卡梅伦·彼得斯 2026年10月1日，晚上10:30 UTC 礼物 2026年9月26日，唐纳德·特朗普在白宫南草坪向媒体挥手致意。Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images 卡梅伦·彼得斯是Vox的专职编辑。本文发表于The Logoff，这是一份每日通讯，帮助你在不让政治新闻占据生活的情况下了解特朗普政府的动态。点此订阅。

##段落
欢迎来到The Logoff：唐纳德·特朗普又一次将接触机会卖给出价最高的人。 发生了什么？ 周四，Washington Sun的杰夫·斯坦报道称，特朗普将在今年晚些时候重启他2025年的“加密货币晚宴”，在他位于弗吉尼亚的高尔夫俱乐部接待$TRUMP迷因币的一些顶级投资者。$TRUMP持有量排名前185的人将收到活动邀请，网站将其描述为“全球最独家的晚宴”。$TRUMP持有量排名前29的人还将有资格参加“特别VIP招待会”。

##段落
什么是$TRUMP？ 正如我的同事亚当·克拉克·埃斯蒂斯去年所解释的那样，像$TRUMP这样的迷因币“几乎是凭空虚构的”。这种币是一种加密代币，或者说是“一种建立在加密货币区块链上的数字资产，但它并不是像比特币那样功能完整的加密货币”。换句话说，购买它并不会让你得到太多东西——自去年年初特朗普上任以来，这种币的价值已经暴跌——但它会给你一个与总统共进晚餐的机会。

##段落
背景是什么？ 这将是特朗普为$TRUMP买家举办的第三场大型活动，此前有2025年5月在他弗吉尼亚俱乐部举行的晚宴，以及今年早些时候在海湖庄园举行的“加密货币与商业会议”，特朗普在会上发表了主旨演讲。但这只是特朗普及其家族发现的众多通过加密货币牟利方式中的一种：还有另一种迷因币$MELANIA，以及他利润丰厚的加密货币公司World Liberty Financial，该公司去年从一名阿联酋王室成员那里获得了5亿美元投资。严格来说，正如斯坦所指出的，特朗普本人并不拥有发行$TRUMP的公司，但他仍从中获利丰厚，去年通过交易费用和其他收入赚取了6.36亿美元。而他从World Liberty Financial赚得更多，该公司由他和他的儿子们以及其他一些人拥有：根据今年早些时候提交的财务披露表格，仅2025年就获利7.99亿美元。

readings.title: Meta's new AI is about to break the internet
body: 21 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Thomas Germain Someday we'll redesign the internet for tools like this. Until then, you're in for a wild ride. Last week, my finger hovered over the download button for Meta's new AI Muse. I felt a little bit scared of my phone. Muse wants to help. It's an AI agent, a tool that goes out into the world for unsupervised tasks. Using its own web browser, Muse can cancel your gym membership, haggle with customer service people, buy groceries, invite friends to parties, you name it. Soon it will make phone calls. It's the first free, full-featured agent from a big company. Millions downloaded Muse in its opening weeks, and OpenAI just announced its own new agent . More are coming. It's the dawn of a new chapter for the web. What will it be like? According to experts I interviewed, the internet is about to get more frustrating. These agents may cause a cascading chain of problems that shake the foundations of digital infrastructure. Chances are good that you're about to live through an era of online chaos.  The internet was built for humans with limited time and patience. AIs don't have those restraints. You'll probably have to fight with robots over concert tickets and booking appointments. Small businesses could drown in machine-made pestering. AIs don't look at ads, and websites that rely on them are already crumbling . You'll be buried in endless loops of proving you're human. And if you use these AI tools, some may betray you. Eventually, we'll rebuild the internet for this new reality. Perhaps that world will be better. Until then, things may get ugly. "Imagine there are no rules of the road. And you release billions of cars – the AI agents – and you just let them drive through playgrounds, hitting kids. That's where we are," says Ramesh Raskar, an associate professor at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in the US who studies AI agents. "It's a pivotal moment." To access the road, Muse arguably asks for more trust and sensitive information than any product in the history of Mark Zuckerberg's empire. When you open it, the cutesy avatar asks for a name. Then it asks for total control of your Gmail, calendar and entire computer if you're on a Mac.  There, staring at the download button, I felt a moment of panic. People begged me to say no. "I wouldn't use it," says Patrick Wardle, co-founder of Objective-See, a US nonprofit security foundation that uncovered serious flaws in the Muse app. "Personally, I would tell you to uninstall it altogether."  Despite the warning, I need to see what Muse users are up against. So I named my AI "Bob", gave it the keys to my life, and stepped into the future.  "Muse is the first personal AI agent built for everyone and designed to be safe, secure and private – with built-in protections and user controls that put people in charge of how they use it," a Meta spokesperson tells me. "Safety and security is a huge priority for us," they said, and added and Muse faced extensive testing . But experts agree there's chaos ahead. If you want a preview of the world that agents may create, look at Taylor Swift. In 2024, some American Swifties flew to Europe to see her. Scalpers, who buy tickets to resell at a mark-up, drove US ticket prices so high it was cheaper to buy flights to international concerts.  Now everyone can have their own personal scalper bot. What we might call the "Swiftie problem" is predicted to explode. "There's going to be a huge escalation of the problems we're already having with bots," says Calli Schroeder, director of the AI and Human Rights Program at the Electronic Privacy Information Center (Epic) in the US. Say goodbye to reservations at that hot new restaurant. Appointments for passport or driver's license renewals in peak travel season? That could be out the window. Some people will probably hoard resources, booking five appointments just in case since it's so effortless. The Interface Worried about an AI apocalypse? Maybe you shouldn't be. Check out the latest episode of The Interface , the BBC's flagship technology podcast. There are solutions to these problems. For example, maybe society abandons "first come first served" and we switch everything to a lottery system. But that would be a paradigm shift compared to life today. "I haven't seen a lot of plans to address these things," says Schoeder. "We're just launching these tools and saying, 'well, we'll deal with the problems when they come up'." Then, of course, there are the instances of "rogue" AI agents hacking governments and companies .  I asked Meta about all of this. On top of complex safety protocols , a Meta spokesperson says Muse asks permission before buying anything and is designed to behave like a "reasonable, honest person" – one who wouldn't, say, buy every ticket to an event, or refresh a page 500 times an hour, according to Meta. Muse is useful. Over the course of a week, I had it reach out to a seller on Facebook Marketplace with questions. The AI ordered the dental floss I like. It negotiated a $31 (£23) discount on a software subscription. Now picture millions or billions of agents doing this all simultaneously, performing multiple tasks that might take weeks for a human to get to. "What happens if bots send 600 inquiries to a website a day, when normal humans might only send two?" says Shroeder. "Businesses and individuals are going to have a lot to deal with." AI is already decimating online business . Google and chatbots now answer questions directly. As a result, people are visiting fewer websites . Robots don't click on ads or buy subscriptions, and it's causing an extinction event for companies across the web. Agents will supercharge this problem.  Meanwhile, one analysis found web traffic from bots spiked 124% in the year to June 2026. Some websites and services are crumbling because they aren't built for that digital load . Meta's spokesperson says Muse works to complete your tasks while respecting the interests of websites. There are also personal risks. "If you're empowering an agent to make things like purchasing decisions, or choices about taste and preferences, you're opening yourself up to being exploited," says Shroeder. If Muse plans your holiday trip, Shroeder says there's no way to know if it got you the best deal, or if it chose flights and hotels that benefit Meta's business partners. If you ask for music recommendations, will they be based on your taste, or will you hear about artists who inked deals with the social media company? Meta's spokesperson says Muse's built-in protections and user controls put people "absolutely in charge" of it, and Muse "behaves like a personal assistant acting for a single person" that follows ethical guidelines to protect users. However, Shroeder says she's examined Muse's terms of service, and there's no guarantee the app will act in your favour.  Raskar, the MIT professor, is part of a growing cohort of researchers and industry insiders designing an internet that works for agents, businesses and people alike. According to Raskar, regulators need a tailored approach to agents. "Think about the models like an engine. The agents are the cars, and that's what we need to regulate," Raskar says. "We need to establish the rules of the road: windshields, brakes, traffic lights and so on." In other words, rules that steer agents' behaviour. The AI industry is developing protocols and standards for bots to plug directly into other services in more cooperative ways. Companies are building systems that would charge AIs a fee if they want to scrape websites. Regulation could force agents to serve users' best interests.  And there are some promising shifts. A few restaurant reservation platforms have banned people for AI misuse. The UK just rewrote the rules for booking driving tests, in part to combat bots. Raskar is optimistic. "Agents could unlock so much investment, innovation and value," he says. We just need to make sure the rules and systems we develop don't give any companies unfair advantages. But the road will be bumpy. And people who use these agents will pay a toll: personal data, perhaps at higher risk than ever before.   Stop for a moment and consider your email inbox. I've had the same Gmail address for 21 years. It's my login for hundreds of accounts. It holds medical test results, contracts and legal documents, conversations with family and endless receipts and financial information. My inbox even has love letters an ex-girlfriend sent, from an era when email (briefly) felt suitable for romance. (I got her permission before handing it to Muse.) More than any other digital service, my email is a window into my brain. Now Meta has it. If that's not enough, Muse also suggested I give it my bank accounts. No thanks. I didn't let the AI run wild on my computer hard drive, either. Meta makes some explicit promises about privacy. The company says it won't connect any of the data Muse collects to its advertising systems. Special systems are supposed to prevent the AI from seeing passwords or payment methods. And when you plug it into Gmail, the AI asks if you want it to scan the whole inbox, or just read messages related to specific tasks.  However, Meta uses your Muse data to train new AI models by default. Shroeder says it's impossible to remove data built into an AI model, and AIs can sometimes be tricked to reveal their training data. Meta says your data is "sanitised" to remove personally identifiable information before it's used for training, and you can opt-out of AI training with a setting. But given Meta's history of privacy problems , should you trust what it's telling you now?  Not according to Wardle from the Objective-See Foundation in the US. Soon after Muse launched, he found a critical vulnerability. "This was literally 20 minutes of me poking at the app, and it just, like, fell over," says Wardle. With a simple hack, he says an attacker could have hijacked Muse, all of its data, and even controlled other devices you connected like your phone or a smart lock. More like this • Is Google about to destroy the web? • The secret codewords that scammers hate • Not on TikTok? They're tracking you anyway   Meta fixed it immediately, but Wardle says the oversight made it impossible for him to trust the company's promises about privacy and safety.  "These bugs were trivial to discover," says Wardle. "If they were willing to ship something that's security was not well vetted, it doesn't give me a warm fuzzy about their intentions." A Meta spokesperson disputes this and says Muse was delayed for months for more privacy and security tests. I spent a lot of time playing with Muse, or "Bob" as I like to call him. It wasn't just useful; I actually enjoyed it. But when I finished writing this article, I revoked Muse's Gmail access and asked the app to erase everything it collected about me. In the end, the fear won out. -- For more insights, sign up to our Tech Decoded newsletter, where Thomas and Lily Jamali break down the biggest stories of the tech world, and help you live a better digital life. Sign up for free here . For more science, technology, environment and health stories from the BBC, follow us on Facebook and Instagram . Technology Keeping Tabs Artificial intelligence Internet Thomas Germain Features

21小时前 分享 保存 在Google上添加为首选 托马斯·杰曼 总有一天，我们会为这类工具重新设计互联网。但在那之前，你将经历一段狂野之旅。上周，我的手指悬停在Meta新款AI Muse的下载按钮上。我对自己的手机感到一丝恐惧。Muse想帮忙。它是一个AI代理，一种能进入外部世界执行无人监督任务的工具。借助自己的网络浏览器，Muse可以帮你取消健身房会员、与客服讨价还价、购买日用品、邀请朋友参加派对，你能想到的它都能做。很快它还将能拨打电话。这是大公司推出的首个免费、功能齐全的代理。Muse在上线头几周就有数百万人下载，而OpenAI也刚刚发布了自己的新代理。更多产品正在路上。这是互联网新篇章的黎明。那会是什么样子？根据我采访的专家说法，互联网即将变得更加令人沮丧。这些代理可能引发一连串问题，动摇数字基础设施的根基。你很有可能即将经历一个网络混乱的时代。

##段落

互联网是为时间有限、耐心有限的人类建造的。AI没有这些限制。你可能不得不为了演唱会门票和预约而与机器人争抢。小企业可能会被机器制造的骚扰淹没。AI不看广告，依赖广告的网站已经在崩塌。你将陷入没完没了的“证明你是人类”的循环中。而如果你使用这些AI工具，有些可能会背叛你。最终，我们会为这个新现实重建互联网。也许那个世界会更好。但在那之前，事情可能会变得很难看。“想象一下，路上没有任何交通规则。你放出数十亿辆车——也就是AI代理——然后任由它们开过游乐场，撞倒孩子。这就是我们现在的处境，”美国麻省理工学院（MIT）研究AI代理的副教授拉梅什·拉斯卡尔说。“这是一个关键时刻。”为了接入这条道路，Muse可以说要求你给予比马克·扎克伯格帝国历史上任何产品都更多的信任和敏感信息。当你打开它时，那个可爱的头像会先问一个名字。然后，如果你用的是Mac，它会要求完全控制你的Gmail、日历和整台电脑。在那里，盯着下载按钮，我感到一阵恐慌。人们求我拒绝。“我不会用它，”美国非营利安全基金会Objective-See的联合创始人帕特里克·沃德尔说。该基金会发现了Muse应用中的严重漏洞。“就我个人而言，我会告诉你直接卸载它。”尽管有警告，我还是需要看看Muse用户面对的是什么。于是我把我的AI命名为“Bob”，把我生活的钥匙交给它，然后迈入了未来。“Muse是首个为所有人打造的个人AI代理，设计上力求安全、可靠且私密……”

##段落
Meta的一位发言人告诉我：“我们内置了保护措施和用户控制功能，让人们可以自主决定如何使用它。”他们表示：“安全与保障对我们来说是重中之重。”并补充说Muse经历了大量测试。但专家们一致认为，混乱即将到来。如果你想预览智能体可能创造的世界，看看泰勒·斯威夫特就知道了。2024年，一些美国“霉粉”飞往欧洲看她的演唱会。黄牛——即买票后加价转售的人——将美国票价炒得极高，以至于买飞往国际演唱会的机票反而更便宜。如今，每个人都可以拥有自己的私人黄牛机器人。我们或许可以称之为“霉霉问题”的现象，预计将呈爆炸式增长。“我们已经在机器人方面遇到的问题，将会急剧升级，”美国电子隐私信息中心（Epic）人工智能与人权项目主任卡莉·施罗德表示。跟那家热门新餐厅的预订说再见吧。在旅行旺季预约护照或驾照续期？那可能也要泡汤了。有些人可能会囤积资源，既然操作如此轻而易举，干脆一口气预约五个名额以防万一。

##段落
The Interface 担心AI末日降临？也许你不必。来看看BBC旗舰科技播客《The Interface》的最新一期。这些问题是有解决方案的。例如，也许社会可以放弃“先到先得”，将一切改为抽签制。但与当今生活相比，那将是一次范式转变。“我还没有看到很多应对这些问题的方案，”施罗德说。“我们只是推出这些工具，然后说‘好吧，等问题出现了再处理’。”当然，还有“失控”AI智能体攻击政府和企业的案例。我就这一切询问了Meta。除了复杂的安全协议外，Meta的一位发言人表示，Muse在购买任何东西之前都会征求许可，并且被设计为表现得像一个“理性、诚实的人”——据Meta所说，这种人不会买下一场活动的所有门票，也不会一小时内刷新页面500次。Muse确实有用。在一周的时间里，我让它联系了Facebook Marketplace上的一位卖家并提问。这个AI订购了我喜欢的牙线。它还在一项软件订阅上谈下了31美元（23英镑）的折扣。现在想象一下，数百万甚至数十亿个智能体同时做这些事，执行多项人类可能需要数周才能完成的任务。“如果机器人每天向一个网站发送600条咨询，而正常人类可能只发送两条，会发生什么？”施罗德说。“企业和个人将面临大量需要处理的事情。”AI已经在大量蚕食在线业务。谷歌和聊天机器人现在直接回答问题。结果是，人们访问的网站越来越少。机器人——

##段落
人们不点击广告，也不购买订阅服务，这正在引发一场席卷全网公司的灭绝事件。AI代理将进一步加剧这个问题。与此同时，一项分析发现，截至2026年6月的一年内，来自机器人的网络流量激增了124%。一些网站和服务正在崩溃，因为它们并非为这种数字负载而构建。Meta的发言人表示，Muse在完成任务的同时会尊重网站的利益。其中也存在个人风险。“如果你授权一个代理去做购买决策，或者决定品味和偏好，你就是在把自己暴露于被利用的风险之中，”施罗德说。如果Muse为你规划假期旅行，施罗德说，你无从得知它是否为你争取到了最优价格，还是选择了有利于Meta商业伙伴的航班和酒店。如果你让它推荐音乐，那些推荐是基于你的品味，还是你会听到与这家社交媒体公司签约的艺人？Meta的发言人表示，Muse的内置保护和用户控制功能让用户“完全掌控”它，Muse“表现得像一个为单个人服务的私人助理”，遵循保护用户的道德准则。然而，施罗德说她仔细查看了Muse的服务条款，并不能保证该应用会以你的利益行事。麻省理工学院的教授拉斯卡尔，属于一个日益壮大的研究者和行业内部人士群体，他们正在设计一个能同时服务于代理、企业和普通人的互联网。据拉斯卡尔所说，监管者需要对代理采取量身定制的方法。“把模型想象成发动机。代理是汽车，那才是我们需要监管的对象，”拉斯卡尔说。“我们需要建立道路规则：挡风玻璃、刹车、红绿灯等等。”换句话说，就是引导代理行为的规则。AI行业正在制定协议和标准，让机器人以更合作的方式直接接入其他服务。企业正在构建系统，如果AI想要抓取网站内容，就向其收取费用。监管可以迫使代理为用户的最佳利益服务。也有一些令人鼓舞的转变。一些餐厅预订平台已经对AI滥用者实施了封禁。英国刚刚重写了驾照考试预约规则，部分原因就是为了打击机器人。拉斯卡尔持乐观态度。“代理可以释放巨大的投资、创新和价值，”他说。我们只需要确保我们制定的规则和系统不会给任何公司带来不公平的优势。但这条路不会平坦。而使用这些代理的人将付出代价：个人数据，可能面临比以往任何时候都更高的风险。

##段落
暂停片刻，想想你的电子邮箱收件箱。我的Gmail地址已经用了21年。它是我数百个账户的登录凭证。里面存着体检结果、合同和法

##段落
法律文件、与家人的对话、无穷无尽的收据和财务信息。我的收件箱里甚至还有前女友寄来的情书，那是一个电子邮件（短暂地）被认为适合谈情说爱的年代。（在把它交给Muse之前，我征得了她的同意。）与其他任何数字服务相比，我的电子邮件更像是窥探我大脑的一扇窗。现在Meta拥有了它。如果这还不够，Muse还建议我把银行账户也交给它。不了，谢谢。我也没有让AI在我的电脑硬盘上肆意妄为。Meta在隐私方面做出了一些明确的承诺。该公司表示，不会将Muse收集的任何数据与其广告系统关联。专门的系统理应阻止AI看到密码或支付方式。当你把它接入Gmail时，AI会询问你是要它扫描整个收件箱，还是只读取与特定任务相关的邮件。然而，Meta默认会使用你的Muse数据来训练新的AI模型。Shroeder表示，一旦数据被内置到AI模型中，就不可能将其移除，而且AI有时会被诱导泄露其训练数据。Meta表示，在数据用于训练之前会经过"净化"处理以去除个人身份信息，并且你可以通过一项设置选择退出AI训练。但鉴于Meta在隐私问题上的历史记录，你现在应该相信它所说的话吗？美国Objective-See基金会的Wardle认为不该相信。Muse发布后不久，他就发现了一个严重漏洞。"我不过是花了20分钟随手试探这个应用，然后它就这么，直接崩了，"Wardle说。他表示，通过一个简单的攻击手段，攻击者本可以劫持Muse、其所有数据，甚至控制你连接的其他设备，比如手机或智能锁。更多类似内容 • 谷歌即将摧毁互联网吗？ • 诈骗分子最怕的秘密暗语 • 不用TikTok？他们照样在追踪你。Meta立即修复了该漏洞，但Wardle表示，这一疏忽让他无法再信任该公司在隐私和安全方面的承诺。"这些漏洞发现起来简直轻而易举，"Wardle说。"如果他们愿意发布一个安全审查如此不到位的产品，那我对他们的意图实在没法放心。"Meta的一位发言人对此提出异议，称Muse因需要更多隐私和安全测试而推迟了数月。我花了很多时间体验Muse，或者我喜欢叫它"Bob"。它不只是有用，我实际上还挺享受使用它的。但当我写完这篇文章后，我撤销了Muse对Gmail的访问权限，并要求该应用删除它收集到的关于我的一切信息。最终，恐惧占了上风。——欲了解更多洞察，请订阅我们的Tech Decoded新闻通讯，Thomas和Lily Jamali将在其中解读科技界的重大新闻，帮助你过上更好的数字生活。在此免费订阅。更多科学、技术

readings.title: Feeling unseen by your boss? Here’s what you can do
body: Feeling unseen by your boss? Here’s what you can do

Ever have your hard work — including your successes — go unnoticed by your manager? Fixable , TED’s new podcast, is here to do just that — to fix the problems of everyday people who call in with their work woes.

In episode four , cohosts and top leadership coaches Frances Frei and Anne Morriss got to know Nai’a, a caller who struggled with receiving recognition after a major reorganization paired her with a new and preoccupied boss. Nai’a was going above and beyond to do her job well, but the lack of acknowledgement and encouragement — and even awareness — of her work was causing her to lose motivation.
Frances’s and Anne’s first piece of advice to Nai’a was simple: See the humanness of what’s going on — and of your manager.

“Sometimes the barrier to showing up as a great collaborator with your manager can be that there’s still some residual frustration about the situation,” Anne explained. “But that emotion is not going to be useful to you.”
Instead, they encouraged Nai’a to recognize the humanity of her manager and forgive them for making mistakes.
Frances and Anne also shared this strategy with her to practice: Choose curiosity over judgment.

Here’s how Frances put it: “You have a choice between judgment and curiosity, because both can’t exist at the same time. So if you have judgment about your manager, you can’t really be curious about their situation. And when you’re thinking of your manager as a person who’s got a lot of part-time jobs, how do we set them up for success?”

“The simplest expression of curiosity — which is truly a magical elixir in a workplace — is in the form of questions,” said Anne. For example, you could start by asking your manager what process works best for them to learn about your accomplishments and contributions. Or, you could focus on how you can make your meetings with them more productive by asking them, “How can our one-on-one time be of service to what we’re trying to achieve together?”

Another option: Be open about your concerns, and ask your manager what their vision of your success looks like. You could say something like, “Here’s my fear: I’m working really hard, and in this state of flux, I’m afraid that six months will go by and people are going to wonder whether or not I did a good job. So it’s just helpful for me to be clear — what is a good job and how can I help in getting that data for you?”

Across industries and across the world, many people are going through workplace reorganizations and other sweeping changes. And like Nai’a, it’s normal to feel anxious and stressed by what’s happening and to need to go through a readjustment period. Leading with questions — and seeing your boss as another human you’re collaborating with — can help you gain back some agency and autonomy.

“Try doing what you can, and marvel at how the other person changes as a result, as opposed to coming up with the list of how you would like the other person to change,” said Frances. “I think you’re going to be pleasantly surprised; that’s the beautiful part of this.”

No matter your job or business, you’ll find actionable advice on Fixable that can improve your workdays. In other episodes, learn how to overcome communication roadblocks, scale up your side project and lead more productive meetings. Plus: Click here for a chance to get your own work question answered on the show! Listen to Fixable now wherever you get your podcasts.
About the author Hayley Caldwell is a copywriter on the Audience Development team at TED.

感觉老板没注意到你？你可以这样做
2023年6月15日
/
Hayley Caldwell
